title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: Wrap data SharedData pipe go_figure(). Formula properties (x = ~gdpPercap) evaluated data, data frame, trace built rows linked: every point carries row’s key. Click point select country: points twelve years highlighted, showing path. Double-click clear; hold shift add countries. key says rows belong together; default data’s row names (one key per row). Views sharing group (default, one per SharedData; set SharedData$new(group = )) linked. Without highlight(), linked figure selects click clears double-click.
code: SharedData$new(gap, key = ~country) |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log")) |>   highlight(color = "red")

what: Several views of the same rows
title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: figure made SharedData, SharedDatas group keys, view selection. 2007’s rows years’ rows linked group “countries”: selecting countries box lasso first plot shows histories second, attrs_selected() draws selected points lines. Clicking point history plot selects country .
code: in_2007 <- SharedData$new(gap[year == 2007], key = ~country, group = "countries") all_years <- SharedData$new(gap, key = ~country, group = "countries")  latest <- in_2007 |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(height = 350, xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log"), title = "Wealth and life expectancy, 2007") |>   highlight(on = "plotly_selected", color = "red")  history <- all_years |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~year, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(height = 350, title = "Life expectancy over time") |>   highlight(color = "red", selected = attrs_selected(mode = "lines+markers"))  htmltools::tagList(as_widget(latest), as_widget(history))

title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: add_<trace>() call links trace one trace’s data arrays (x, y, z, values, ids, …) one value per row SharedData. traces, summaries reference lines, stay unlinked unchanged selections: SharedData can also given single trace data:
code: world <- gap[, .(lifeExp = weighted.mean(lifeExp, pop)), by = year] #> Warning in gsum(w, na.rm = FALSE): The sum of an integer column for a group was #> more than type 'integer' can hold so the result has been coerced to 'numeric' #> automatically for convenience.  SharedData$new(gap, key = ~country) |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~year, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers", name = "countries") |>   add_scatter(x = world$year, y = world$lifeExp, mode = "lines", name = "world") |>   highlight(color = "red", selected = attrs_selected(mode = "lines+markers")) go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~year, y = ~lifeExp, data = all_years, mode = "markers") |>  # linked   add_scatter(x = ~year, y = ~pop, data = gap, mode = "markers")                # not linked

what: Linking traces built from other data
title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: set_crosstalk_keys() links traces whose values don’t come SharedData’s rows, summaries: give keys trace’s points group join. points keyed continent, bar chart countries per continent linked , clicking bar selects every country continent (clicking point selects continent): simple = TRUE, trace stands keys whole, marks can’t split points, line summarising group. continent’s average life expectancy line standing countries: clicking line selects plot . line highlighted countries selected.
code: by_continent <- SharedData$new(gap, key = ~continent) countries <- gap[year == 2007, .N, by = continent]  continent_bars <- go_figure() |>   add_bar(x = countries$continent, y = countries$N) |>   set_crosstalk_keys(countries$continent, group = by_continent$groupName()) |>   update_layout(height = 300, yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "countries")) |>   highlight(color = "red")  continent_points <- by_continent |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(height = 350, xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log")) |>   highlight(color = "red")  htmltools::tagList(as_widget(continent_bars), as_widget(continent_points)) by_country2 <- SharedData$new(gap, key = ~country)  averages <- go_figure() for (cont in sort(unique(gap$continent))) {   d <- gap[continent == cont, .(lifeExp = mean(lifeExp)), by = year]   averages <- averages |>     add_scatter(x = d$year, y = d$lifeExp, mode = "lines+markers", name = cont) |>     set_crosstalk_keys(unique(gap[continent == cont, country]),                        group = by_country2$groupName(),                        traces = length(averages$data) + 1L, simple = TRUE) } # plotly.js reports clicks on a line's points: let a click near the line count averages <- averages |>   update_layout(height = 350, hoverdistance = 50, title = "Average by continent") |>   highlight(color = "red")  country_points <- by_country2 |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~year, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(height = 300, title = "Countries") |>   highlight(color = "red")  htmltools::tagList(as_widget(averages), as_widget(country_points))

title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: crosstalk’s filter inputs subset every view SharedData’s group: traces show rows pass filters. Filters work keys (key passes rows ), filter year key per row, default:
code: filtered <- SharedData$new(gap) htmltools::tagList(   filter_checkbox("continent", "Continent", filtered, ~continent, inline = TRUE),   filter_slider("year", "Year", filtered, ~year, width = "100%", sep = ""),   filtered |>     go_figure() |>     add_scatter(x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>     update_layout(height = 350, xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log")) |>     as_widget() )

title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: Subplots: traces added several cells (add_scatter(..., row = 1, col = "")) linked. set_crosstalk_keys() uses trace indices, call adding traces links. Animation: animation frame’s traces carry keys, set set_crosstalk_keys(). widgets: crosstalk-compatible widget, DT tables leaflet maps, can share group. Trace types: selection events need traces points (scatter, bar, histogram, box, maps, …); plotly.js reports clicks hovers line’s points, . Heatmaps, pies aggregating traces can’t selected point point. Shiny: crosstalk works without server; Shiny, event_data() also reports selections, SharedData selections can read <SharedData>$selection(). Size: keys sent strings, one per point; many thousands points, short keys keep pages small.

title: 3D Hover Options
text: default, Plotly’s 3D plots display lines called “spikelines” hovering point. lines project hover point three axes’ normal planes extend projection data points planes’ wall boundaries.
code: library(plotly.core)  mtcars$am[which(mtcars$am == 0)] <- "Automatic" mtcars$am[which(mtcars$am == 1)] <- "Manual" mtcars$am <- as.factor(mtcars$am)  am_colors <- c(Automatic = "#BF382A", Manual = "#0C4B8E")  mtcars |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = am_colors) |>   add_scatter3d(     x = ~wt,     y = ~hp,     z = ~qsec,     mode = "markers",     opacity = 0.8,     marker = go_scatter3d_marker(color = ~am)   ) |>   update_layout(     scene = go_scene(       xaxis = go_scene_axis(         spikecolor = "#a009b5",         spikesides = FALSE,         spikethickness = 6       ),       yaxis = go_scene_axis(         spikecolor = "#a009b5",         spikesides = FALSE,         spikethickness = 6       ),       zaxis = go_scene_axis(         spikecolor = "#a009b5",         spikethickness = 6       )     )   )

title: 3D Line Plots
code: library(plotly.core)  x <- c() y <- c() z <- c() c <- c()  for (i in 1:62) {   r <- 20 * cos(i / 20)   x <- c(x, r * cos(i))   y <- c(y, r * sin(i))   z <- c(z, i)   c <- c(c, i) }  data <- data.frame(x, y, z, c)  data |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter3d(     x = ~x,     y = ~y,     z = ~z,     mode = "lines+markers",     line = go_scatter3d_line(width = 6, color = ~c, colorscale = "Viridis"),     marker = go_scatter3d_marker(       size = 3.5,       color = ~c,       colorscale = "Greens",       cmin = -20,       cmax = 50     )   )

title: Intro to Animations
code: library(plotly.core)  df <- data.frame(   x = c(1,2,1),    y = c(1,2,1),    f = c(1,2,3) )  fig <- df[df$f == 1, ] |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~x, y = ~y, mode = "markers", showlegend = FALSE)  fig$frames <- lapply(df$f, function(f) {   list(     name = as.character(f),     data = list(go_scatter(x = df$x[df$f == f], y = df$y[df$f == f]))   ) })  fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(range = c(0.9, 2.1)),     yaxis = go_yaxis(range = c(0.9, 2.1)),     updatemenus = list(       go_updatemenu(         type = "buttons",         showactive = FALSE,         x = 0,         y = 0,         yanchor = "top",         pad = go_updatemenu_pad(t = 60, r = 10),         xanchor = "right",         buttons = list(           go_updatemenu_button(             label = "Play",             method = "animate",             args = list(NULL, list(fromcurrent = TRUE, mode = "immediate"))           )         )       )     ),     sliders = list(       go_slider(         pad = go_slider_pad(t = 50),         steps = lapply(df$f, function(f) {           go_slider_step(             label = as.character(f),             method = "animate",             args = list(list(as.character(f)), list(mode = "immediate"))           )         })       )     )   )  fig

title: Intro to Animations
text: One trace per continent, one frame per year holding values every trace year. play_button() year_slider() build animation controls; following sections change options.
code: library(plotly.core) library(gapminder)  df <- as.data.frame(gapminder) years <- sort(unique(df$year)) continents <- levels(df$continent) # marker area proportional to population sizeref <- 2 * max(df$pop) / 60^2  continent_trace <- function(d) {   go_scatter(     x = d$gdpPercap,     y = d$lifeExp,     text = d$country,     marker = go_scatter_marker(size = d$pop, sizemode = "area", sizeref = sizeref)   ) }  fig <- df[df$year == years[1], ] |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     x = ~gdpPercap,     y = ~lifeExp,     text = ~country,     hoverinfo = "text",     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(       color = ~continent,       size = ~pop,       sizemode = "area",       sizeref = sizeref     )   )  fig$frames <- lapply(years, function(yr) {   list(     name = as.character(yr),     data = lapply(continents, function(cont) {       continent_trace(df[df$continent == cont & df$year == yr, ])     })   ) })  animation_args <- function(frames, duration, easing) {   list(     frames,     list(       frame = list(duration = duration, redraw = FALSE),       transition = list(duration = duration, easing = easing),       fromcurrent = TRUE,       mode = "immediate"     )   ) }  play_button <- function(duration = 500, easing = "linear", ...) {   go_updatemenu(     type = "buttons",     showactive = FALSE,     ...,     buttons = list(       go_updatemenu_button(         label = "Play",         method = "animate",         args = animation_args(NULL, duration, easing)       )     )   ) }  year_slider <- function(duration = 500, easing = "linear", ...) {   go_slider(     pad = go_slider_pad(t = 50),     ...,     steps = lapply(years, function(yr) {       go_slider_step(         label = as.character(yr),         method = "animate",         args = animation_args(list(as.character(yr)), duration, easing)       )     })   ) }  fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log", range = log10(range(df$gdpPercap)) + c(-0.1, 0.1)),     yaxis = go_yaxis(range = range(df$lifeExp) + c(-5, 5)),     updatemenus = list(       play_button(x = 0, xanchor = "right", y = 0, yanchor = "top", pad = go_updatemenu_pad(t = 60, r = 10))     ),     sliders = list(year_slider())   )  fig

what: Choosing The Algorithm For Computing Quartiles
title: Box Plots
text: default, quartiles box plots computed using linear method (linear interpolation, see #10 listed http://www.amstat.org/publications/jse/v14n3/langford.html https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quartile details). However, can also choose use exclusive inclusive algorithm compute quartiles. exclusive algorithm uses median divide ordered dataset two halves. sample odd, include median either half. Q1 median lower half Q3 median upper half. inclusive algorithm also uses median divide ordered dataset two halves, sample odd, includes median halves. Q1 median lower half Q3 median upper half.

title: Bubble Charts
text: scale bubble size, use attribute sizeref. recommend using following formula calculate sizeref value: sizeref = 2. * max(array size values) / (desired maximum marker size ** 2)  Note setting sizeref value greater 1 decreases rendered marker sizes, setting sizeref less 1 increases rendered marker sizes. See go_scatter_marker() information.  Additionally, recommend setting sizemode attribute area.
code: library(plotly.core)  data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv")  data$State <- as.factor(c('Massachusetts', 'California', 'Massachusetts', 'Pennsylvania', 'New Jersey', 'Illinois', 'Washington DC',                           'Massachusetts', 'Connecticut', 'New York', 'North Carolina', 'New Hampshire', 'New York', 'Indiana',                           'New York', 'Michigan', 'Rhode Island', 'California', 'Georgia', 'California', 'California'))  # One color per state, interpolated from the "Paired" palette state_colors <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(nlevels(data$State))  #Use the ideal sizeref value desired_maximum_marker_size <- 40 your_list_of_size_values <- data['Gap'] sizeref <- 2.0 * max(your_list_of_size_values) / (desired_maximum_marker_size**2)  data |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = state_colors) |>   add_scatter(     x = ~Women,     y = ~Men,     text = ~School,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(       size = ~Gap,       opacity = 0.5,       sizemode = "area",       sizeref = sizeref,       color = ~State     )   ) |>   update_layout(     title = "Gender Gap in Earnings per University",     xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE),     yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE),     showlegend = FALSE   )

title: Bullet Charts
text: Stephen ’s Bullet Chart invented replace dashboard gauges meters, combining types charts simple bar charts qualitative bars (steps), quantitative bar (bar) performance line (threshold); one simple layout. Steps typically broken several values, defined array. bar represent actual value particular variable reached, threshold usually indicate goal point relative value achieved bar. See indicator page detail.
code: library(plotly.core)  go_figure() |>   add_indicator(     mode = "number+gauge+delta",     gauge = go_indicator_gauge(shape = "bullet"),     delta = go_indicator_delta(reference = 300),     value = 220,     domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)),     title = go_indicator_title(text = "Profit")   ) |>   update_layout(height = 150)

title: Bullet Charts
text: example using “steps” attribute, shown shading, “threshold” determine boundaries visually alert value cross defined threshold.

title: Bullet Charts
text: Bullet charts can stacked comparing several values illustrated :
code: library(plotly.core)  bullet_gauge <- function(range_max, threshold, steps) {   go_indicator_gauge(     shape = "bullet",     axis = go_indicator_gauge_axis(range = c(NA, range_max)),     threshold = go_indicator_gauge_threshold(       line = go_indicator_gauge_threshold_line(color = "black", width = 2),       thickness = 0.75,       value = threshold     ),     steps = list(       go_indicator_gauge_step(range = c(0, steps[[1]]), color = "gray"),       go_indicator_gauge_step(range = steps, color = "lightgray")     ),     bar = go_indicator_gauge_bar(color = "black")   ) }  go_figure() |>   add_indicator(     mode = "number+gauge+delta",     value = 180,     delta = go_indicator_delta(reference = 200),     domain = go_domain(x = c(0.25, 1), y = c(0.08, 0.25)),     title = go_indicator_title(text = "Revenue"),     gauge = bullet_gauge(300, 170, c(150, 250))   ) |>   add_indicator(     mode = "number+gauge+delta",     value = 35,     delta = go_indicator_delta(reference = 200),     domain = go_domain(x = c(0.25, 1), y = c(0.4, 0.6)),     title = go_indicator_title(text = "Profit"),     gauge = bullet_gauge(100, 50, c(25, 75))   ) |>   add_indicator(     mode = "number+gauge+delta",     value = 220,     delta = go_indicator_delta(reference = 300),     domain = go_domain(x = c(0.25, 1), y = c(0.7, 0.9)),     title = go_indicator_title(text = "Satisfaction"),     gauge = bullet_gauge(300, 210, c(100, 250))   )

title: Candlestick Charts
text: segment line two points, NAs segments break line.
code: library(plotly.core)  dat <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv") names(dat) <- sub("^AAPL\\.", "", names(dat)) dat <- subset(dat, Date >= "2016-01-01")  # x and y of the segments from y0 to y1, one per row, separated by NAs segments <- function(d, y0, y1) {   list(     x = as.vector(rbind(d$Date, d$Date, NA)),     y = as.vector(rbind(d[[y0]], d[[y1]], NA))   ) }  directions <- c(Decreasing = "red", Increasing = "forestgreen")  fig <- go_figure() for (dir in names(directions)) {   d <- dat[dat$direction == dir, ]   low_high <- segments(d, "Low", "High")   open_close <- segments(d, "Open", "Close")   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       x = low_high$x,       y = low_high$y,       mode = "lines",       line = go_scatter_line(color = directions[[dir]], width = 1),       hoverinfo = "none"     ) |>     add_scatter(       x = open_close$x,       y = open_close$y,       mode = "lines",       line = go_scatter_line(color = directions[[dir]], width = 3),       hoverinfo = "none"     ) } fig <- fig |>   update_layout(showlegend = FALSE, yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Price")) |>   update_xaxes(rangeslider = go_xaxis_rangeslider(visible = TRUE))  fig

title: Candlestick Charts
text: data set already holds Bollinger bands (dn, mavg, ) direction day. #Reference See go_candlestick() information chart attribute options!
code: library(plotly.core)  df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv") df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)  band_line <- go_scatter_line(color = "#ccc", width = 0.5) direction_colors <- c(Increasing = "#17BECF", Decreasing = "#7F7F7F")  i <- go_candlestick_increasing(line = go_candlestick_increasing_line(color = "#17BECF")) d <- go_candlestick_decreasing(line = go_candlestick_decreasing_line(color = "#7F7F7F"))  # subplot with shared x axis fig <- make_subplots(   rows = 2,   cols = 1,   shared_xaxes = TRUE,   row_heights = c(0.7, 0.2) )  # plot candlestick chart fig <- fig |>   add_candlestick(     data = df,     x = ~Date,     open = ~AAPL.Open,     close = ~AAPL.Close,     high = ~AAPL.High,     low = ~AAPL.Low,     name = "AAPL",     increasing = i,     decreasing = d,     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = df,     x = ~Date,     y = ~up,     name = "B Bands",     mode = "lines",     line = band_line,     legendgroup = "Bollinger Bands",     hoverinfo = "none",     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = df,     x = ~Date,     y = ~dn,     name = "B Bands",     mode = "lines",     line = band_line,     legendgroup = "Bollinger Bands",     showlegend = FALSE,     hoverinfo = "none",     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = df,     x = ~Date,     y = ~mavg,     name = "Mv Avg",     mode = "lines",     line = go_scatter_line(color = "#E377C2", width = 0.5),     hoverinfo = "none",     row = 1,     col = 1   )  # plot volume bar chart for (dir in names(direction_colors)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_bar(       data = df[df$direction == dir, ],       x = ~Date,       y = ~AAPL.Volume,       name = dir,       marker = go_bar_marker(color = direction_colors[[dir]]),       row = 2,       col = 1     ) }  # create rangeselector buttons rs <- go_xaxis_rangeselector(   visible = TRUE,   x = 0.5,   y = -0.055,   xanchor = "center",   font = go_font(size = 9),   buttons = list(     go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(count = 1, label = "RESET", step = "all"),     go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(       count = 1,       label = "1 YR",       step = "year",       stepmode = "backward"     ),     go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(       count = 3,       label = "3 MO",       step = "month",       stepmode = "backward"     ),     go_xaxis_rangeselector_button(       count = 1,       label = "1 MO",       step = "month",       stepmode = "backward"     )   ) )  fig <- fig |>   update_yaxes(title = "Price", row = 1, col = 1) |>   update_yaxes(title = "Volume", row = 2, col = 1) |>   update_xaxes(     rangeselector = rs,     rangeslider = go_xaxis_rangeslider(visible = FALSE),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   update_layout(     title = "Apple: 2015-02-17 - 2017-02-16",     legend = go_legend(       orientation = "h",       x = 0.5,       y = 1,       xanchor = "center",       yref = "paper",       font = go_font(size = 10),       bgcolor = "transparent"     )   )  fig

code: library(plotly.core) library(jsonlite)  url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json" counties <- fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE) url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv" df <- read.csv(url2, colClasses = c(fips = "character")) g <- go_geo(   scope = "usa",   projection = go_geo_projection(type = "albers usa"),   showlakes = TRUE,   lakecolor = "white" )  go_figure() |>   add_choropleth(     geojson = counties,     locations = df$fips,     z = df$unemp,     colorscale = "Viridis",     zmin = 0,     zmax = 12,     marker = go_choropleth_marker(line = go_choropleth_marker_line(width = 0)),     colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "Unemployment Rate (%)")   ) |>   update_layout(title = "2016 US Unemployment by County", geo = g)

text: example based r-statistics post.
code: library(plotly.core) library(stringr) library(reshape2)  data.loess <- loess(qsec ~ wt * hp, data = mtcars)  # Create a sequence of incrementally increasing (by 0.3 units) values for both wt and hp xgrid <-  seq(min(mtcars$wt), max(mtcars$wt), 0.3) ygrid <-  seq(min(mtcars$hp), max(mtcars$hp), 0.3) # Generate a dataframe with every possible combination of wt and hp data.fit <-  expand.grid(wt = xgrid, hp = ygrid) # Feed the dataframe into the loess model and receive a matrix output with estimates of # acceleration for each combination of wt and hp mtrx3d <-  predict(data.loess, newdata = data.fit) # Abbreviated display of final matrix mtrx3d[1:4, 1:4] ##           hp ## wt         hp= 52.0 hp= 52.3 hp= 52.6 hp= 52.9 ##   wt=1.513 19.04237 19.03263 19.02285 19.01302 ##   wt=1.813 19.25566 19.24637 19.23703 19.22764 ##   wt=2.113 19.55298 19.54418 19.53534 19.52645 ##   wt=2.413 20.06436 20.05761 20.05077 20.04383 # Transform data to long form mtrx.melt <- melt(mtrx3d, id.vars = c('wt', 'hp'), measure.vars = 'qsec') names(mtrx.melt) <- c('wt', 'hp', 'qsec') # Return data to numeric form mtrx.melt$wt <- as.numeric(str_sub(mtrx.melt$wt, str_locate(mtrx.melt$wt, '=')[1,1] + 1)) mtrx.melt$hp <-  as.numeric(str_sub(mtrx.melt$hp, str_locate(mtrx.melt$hp, '=')[1,1] + 1))  mtrx.melt |>   go_figure() |>   add_contour(x = ~wt, y = ~hp, z = ~qsec) |>   update_layout(width = 600, height = 500)

title: Creating and Updating Figures
text: go_*() functions (go_figure(), go_bar(), go_bar_marker(), go_layout(), go_xaxis(), …) provide automatically-generated hierarchy classes may used represent figures. Graph objects several benefits compared plain R lists. Graph objects provide precise data validation. provide invalid property name invalid property value, error raised helpful message describing problem. Graph objects contain descriptions valid property R documentation. can use help pages (e.g. ?go_bar) learn available properties alternative consulting online Full Reference. Properties graph objects can accessed using list-style lookup (e.g. fig$data[[1]]$x). Figures support higher-level convenience functions making updates already constructed figures (update_layout(), add_trace(), update_traces(), etc). Figures can displayed directly, saved HTML write_html() exported static images save_image(). can find example one way figure example specified using graph objects instead list.
code: library(plotly.core)  go_figure() |>   add_bar(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(1, 3, 2)) |>   update_layout(     title = "A Plotly Figure",     plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6",     xaxis = go_xaxis(zerolinecolor = "#ffff", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "#ffff"),     yaxis = go_yaxis(zerolinecolor = "#ffff", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "#ffff")   )

title: Creating and Updating Figures
text: figure update operations described functions return modified figure. makes possible chain multiple figure modification operations together single expression pipe. example chained expression : sets title font size using layout.title.font.size, disables vertical grid lines using update_xaxes(), updates size color markers bar using update_traces(), displaying figure.
code: library(plotly.core)  t <- go_font(size = 15)  go_figure() |>   add_bar(x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(2, 1, 3), name = "b", marker = go_bar_marker(color = "red")) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(0, 1, 2),     y = c(4, 2, 3.5),     mode = "markers",     name = "a",     marker = go_scatter_marker(size = 10, color = "rgb(51, 204, 51)")   ) |>   # updates the size and color of the markers and bar   update_traces(marker = go_scatter_marker(size = 20, color = "blue"), selector = "scatter") |>   update_traces(     marker = go_bar_marker(       color = "yellow",       line = go_bar_marker_line(color = "rgb(8,48,107)", width = 1.5)     ),     selector = "bar"   ) |>   update_layout(     title = go_layout_title(       text = "Chaining Multiple Figure Operations With A Plotly Figure",       # setting the title font size       font = t     ),     plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6"   ) |>   # disables vertical grid lines   update_xaxes(showgrid = FALSE, zerolinecolor = "#ffff", zerolinewidth = 2) |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "#ffff", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "#ffff") # displaying the figure

title: Cumulative Animations
code: library(plotly.core) library(dplyr)  df <- ggplot2::txhousing |>   filter(year > 2005, city %in% c("Abilene", "Bay Area")) dates <- sort(unique(df$date)) cities <- unique(df$city)  # The data shown at each step: every row up to and including that date accumulate_to <- function(d) {   lapply(cities, function(cty) df[df$city == cty & df$date <= d, ]) }  fig <- go_figure() first <- accumulate_to(dates[1]) for (k in seq_along(cities)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       x = first[[k]]$date,       y = first[[k]]$median,       mode = "lines",       name = cities[k]     ) }  fig$frames <- lapply(dates, function(d) {   list(     name = as.character(d),     data = lapply(accumulate_to(d), function(sub) {       go_scatter(x = sub$date, y = sub$median)     })   ) })  fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(       title = "Date",       zeroline = FALSE,       range = range(dates)     ),     yaxis = go_yaxis(       title = "Median",       zeroline = FALSE,       range = range(df$median, na.rm = TRUE)     ),     updatemenus = list(       go_updatemenu(         type = "buttons",         showactive = FALSE,         x = 1,         xanchor = "right",         y = 0,         yanchor = "bottom",         buttons = list(           go_updatemenu_button(             label = "Play",             method = "animate",             args = list(               NULL,               list(                 frame = list(duration = 100, redraw = FALSE),                 transition = list(duration = 0),                 fromcurrent = TRUE,                 mode = "immediate"               )             )           )         )       )     )   )  fig

code: library(plotly.core)  x0 <- rnorm(400, mean = 2, sd = 0.4) y0 <- rnorm(400, mean = 2, sd = 0.4) x1 <- rnorm(400, mean = 3, sd = 0.6) y1 <- rnorm(400, mean = 6, sd = 0.4) x2 <- rnorm(400, mean = 4, sd = 0.2) y2 <- rnorm(400, mean = 4, sd = 0.4)  # shapes components cluster_shape <- function(x, y, color) {   go_shape(     type = "circle",     xref = "x",     yref = "y",     x0 = min(x),     y0 = min(y),     x1 = max(x),     y1 = max(y),     opacity = 0.25,     line = go_shape_line(color = color),     fillcolor = color   ) } cluster0 <- cluster_shape(x0, y0, "#835AF1") cluster1 <- cluster_shape(x1, y1, "#7FA6EE") cluster2 <- cluster_shape(x2, y2, "#B8F7D4")  shapes_button <- function(label, shapes) {   go_updatemenu_button(     label = label,     method = "relayout",     args = list(list(shapes = shapes))   ) }  # updatemenus component updatemenus <- list(   go_updatemenu(     active = -1,     type = "buttons",     buttons = list(       shapes_button("None", list()),       shapes_button("Cluster 0", list(cluster0)),       shapes_button("Cluster 1", list(cluster1)),       shapes_button("Cluster 2", list(cluster2)),       shapes_button("All", list(cluster0, cluster1, cluster2))     )   ) )  go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     x = x0,     y = y0,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#835AF1")   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = x1,     y = y1,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#7FA6EE")   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = x2,     y = y2,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#B8F7D4")   ) |>   update_layout(     title = "Highlight Clusters",     showlegend = FALSE,     updatemenus = updatemenus   )

code: library(plotly.core)  # read in wind turbines data df_wind <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.r-docs/master/r/data/2805.csv")  # subset and clean data df_sub <- subset(df_wind, manufac != "unknown", select = c(lat_DD, long_DD, manufac))  # the largest wind farms (by number of turbines), at their median location df_farms <- subset(df_wind, !grepl("^unknown", site_name)) df_farms <- aggregate(   cbind(Latitude = lat_DD, Longitude = long_DD) ~ site_name,   data = df_farms,   FUN = median ) turbines <- table(df_wind$site_name) df_farms$turbines <- as.vector(turbines[df_farms$site_name]) df_farms <- df_farms[order(-df_farms$turbines), ] df_farms$Wind.Farm <- df_farms$site_name rm(df_wind)  # location buttons usa <- go_updatemenu_button(   method = "relayout",   args = list(list(     map.center.lat = median(df_sub$lat_DD),     map.center.lon = median(df_sub$long_DD),     map.zoom = 3   )),   label = "USA" )  buttons <- function(i) {   go_updatemenu_button(     method = "relayout",     args = list(list(       map.center.lat = df_farms$Latitude[i],       map.center.lon = df_farms$Longitude[i],       map.zoom = 9     )),     label = df_farms$Wind.Farm[i]   ) }  # map style buttons style_button <- function(style, label) {   go_updatemenu_button(     method = "relayout",     args = list(list(map.style = style)),     label = label   ) } basic <- style_button("carto-voyager", "Basic") dark <- style_button("carto-darkmatter", "Dark") satellite <- style_button("satellite", "Satellite")  # plot one scattermap trace per manufacturer, with buttons df_sub |>   go_figure() |>   add_scattermap(     lat = ~lat_DD,     lon = ~long_DD,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scattermap_marker(size = 3),     split = ~manufac   ) |>   add_annotation(     x = 0.05,     y = 0.05,     text = "All US wind turbines (scroll to zoom)",     xref = "paper",     yref = "paper",     showarrow = FALSE,     font = go_font(color = "magenta", size = 14)   ) |>   update_layout(     plot_bgcolor = "black",     paper_bgcolor = "black",     map = go_map(       center = go_map_center(         lat = median(df_sub$lat_DD),         lon = median(df_sub$long_DD)       ),       zoom = 3,       style = "carto-darkmatter"     ),     updatemenus = list(       go_updatemenu(         type = "buttons",         direction = "right",         xanchor = "center",         yanchor = "top",         pad = go_updatemenu_pad(r = 0, t = 10, b = 10),         x = 0.5,         y = 1,         showactive = FALSE,         buttons = list(usa, buttons(1), buttons(2), buttons(3), buttons(4))       ),       go_updatemenu(         type = "buttons",         direction = "right",         xanchor = "center",         yanchor = "top",         pad = go_updatemenu_pad(r = 0, t = 10, b = 10),         x = 0.5,         y = 0.935,         showactive = FALSE,         buttons = list(buttons(6), buttons(7), buttons(8), buttons(9))       ),       go_updatemenu(         type = "buttons",         direction = "right",         yanchor = "bottom",         x = 1,         y = 0,         buttons = list(dark, basic, satellite)       )     )   )

title: The Figure Data Structure
text: plotly.core R package making interactive, publication-quality graphs: line plots, scatter plots, area charts, bar charts, error bars, box plots, histograms, heatmaps, subplots, multiple-axes, 3D (WebGL based) charts. free open source can view source, report issues contribute GitHub. rendering process uses Plotly.js JavaScript library hood. Figures represented R go_figure objects: nested lists typed graph objects (go_scatter(), go_layout(), go_xaxis(), …), serialized text JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) passed Plotly.js. Viewing underlying data structure figure can done str(), JSON sent Plotly.js plotly_json(fig).

title: The Figure Data Structure
text: Plotly.js supports inputs adhering well-defined schema, whose overall architecture explained page exhaustively documented Figure Reference (generated machine-readable JSON representation schema). Figures represented trees named nodes called “attributes”. Attributes referred text Figure Reference names. example layout$width refers attribute whose key "width" inside list value associated key "layout" root figure. manipulating go_figure object, attributes can set directly R list assignment, e.g. fig$layout$title$font$family <- "Open Sans", using fig |> update_layout(title = go_layout_title(font = go_font(family = "Open Sans"))). building figure, necessary populate every attribute every object. render-time, JavaScript layer compute default values required unspecified attribute, depending upon ones specified, documented Figure Reference. example layout.xaxis.range, may specified explicitly, computed based range x values every trace linked axis. JavaScript layer ignore unknown attributes malformed values, although plotly.core validates every attribute R figure built, reports invalid properties error naming valid ones.

title: The Figure Data Structure
text: first three top-level attributes figure data, whose value must list referred “traces”. trace one 40 possible types (see list organized subplot type, including e.g. scatter, bar, pie, surface, choropleth etc), represents set related graphical marks figure. trace must type attribute defines allowable attributes. trace drawn single subplot whose type must compatible trace’s type, subplot (see ). Traces may single legend entry, exception pie funnelarea traces (see ). Certain trace types support continuous color, associated colorbar, can controlled attributes either within trace, within layout using coloraxis attribute (see go_coloraxis()).

title: The Figure Data Structure

what: Positioning With Paper, Container Coordinates, or Axis Domain Coordinates
title: The Figure Data Structure
text: Various figure components configured within layout figure support positioning attributes named x y, whose values may specified “paper coordinates” (sometimes referred “plot fractions” “normalized coordinates”). Examples include layout.xaxis.domain layout.legend.x layout.annotation.x. Positioning paper coordinates done absolute pixel terms, rather terms relative coordinate system defined origin (0,0) (layout.margin.l, layout.margin.b) point (1,1) (layout.width-layout.margin.r, layout.height-layout.margin.t) (note: layout.margin values pixel values, layout.width layout.height). Paper coordinate values less 0 greater 1 permitted, refer areas within plot margins. position object “paper” coordinates, corresponding axis reference set "paper". instance shape’s xref attribute set "paper" x value shape refers position paper coordinates. Note contents layout.margin attribute default computed based position dimensions certain items like title legend, may made dependent position dimensions tick labels well setting layout.xaxis.automargin attribute True. effect automatically increasing margin values therefore shrinking physical area defined (0,0) (1,1) points. Positioning certain items paper coordinates less 0 greater 1 also trigger behavior. layout.width layout.height, however, taken givens, figure never grow shrink based contents. figure title may positioned using “container coordinates” (0,0) (1,1) anchored bottom-left top-right figure, respectively, therefore independent values layout.margin. Furthermore, shapes, annotations, images can placed relative axis’s domain , instance, x value 0.5 place object halfway along x-axis, regardless domain specified layout.xaxis.domain attribute. behavior can specified adding ' domain' axis reference axis referencing attribute object. example, setting yref = 'y2 domain' shape refer length position axis named y2.

code: library(plotly.core) data("iris")  hline <- function(y = 0, color = "black") {   go_shape(     type = "line",     x0 = 0,     x1 = 1,     xref = "paper",     y0 = y,     y1 = y,     line = go_shape_line(color = color)   ) }  iris |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~Petal.Length, y = ~Petal.Width, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(     shapes = list(       hline(0.9),       go_shape(type = "rect", line = go_shape_line(color = "black"), x0 = 0.9, x1 = 2)     ),     plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6"   ) library(plotly.core) data("iris")  vline <- function(x = 0, color = "green") {   go_shape(     type = "line",     y0 = 0,     y1 = 1,     yref = "paper",     x0 = x,     x1 = x,     line = go_shape_line(color = color, dash = "dot")   ) }  iris |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~Petal.Length, y = ~Petal.Width, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(     plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6",     shapes = list(       vline(2.5),       go_shape(         type = "rect",         fillcolor = "red",         line = go_shape_line(color = "red"),         opacity = 0.2,         y0 = 0.9,         y1 = 2.6,         x0 = 0.5,         x1 = 7.5       )     )   )

title: kNN Classification
text: Now, train kNN model training data displayed previous graph. , predict confidence score model data points test set. use shapes denote true labels, color indicate confidence model assign score. label gets trace (symbol), traces share continuous color scale based yscore output kNN model.
code: library(plotly.core) library(class)  make_moons <- read.csv(file = "data/make_moons.csv") make_moons$y <- as.character(make_moons$y) set.seed(123) train_index <- sample(nrow(make_moons), 3/4 * nrow(make_moons)) make_moons$split <- "Test Split Label" make_moons$split[train_index] <- "Train Split Label"  # kNN score: the fraction of the k nearest training samples labelled "1" knn_score <- function(train, test, labels, k = 15) {   pred <- knn(train, test, labels, k = k, prob = TRUE)   ifelse(pred == "1", attr(pred, "prob"), 1 - attr(pred, "prob")) }  train_data <- make_moons[make_moons$split == "Train Split Label", ] pdb <- make_moons[make_moons$split == "Test Split Label", ] pdb$yscore <- knn_score(   train_data[, c("X1", "X2")],   pdb[, c("X1", "X2")],   train_data$y,   k = 15 )  label_symbols <- c("0" = "square-dot", "1" = "circle-dot")  fig <- go_figure() for (lab in names(label_symbols)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       data = pdb[pdb$y == lab, ],       x = ~X1,       y = ~X2,       mode = "markers",       name = lab,       marker = go_scatter_marker(         symbol = label_symbols[[lab]],         size = 12,         color = ~yscore,         colorscale = "RdBu",         cmin = 0,         cmax = 1,         showscale = lab == "1",         colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "yscore"),         line = go_scatter_marker_line(color = "black", width = 1)       )     ) }  fig

attr(pred, "prob")) }  mesh_size <- .02 margin <- 0.25 x_min <- min(make_moons$X1) - margin x_max <- max(make_moons$X1) + margin y_min <- min(make_moons$X2) - margin y_max <- max(make_moons$X2) + margin xrange <- seq(x_min, x_max, mesh_size) yrange <- seq(y_min, y_max, mesh_size) xy <- meshgrid(x = xrange, y = yrange) xx <- xy$X yy <- xy$Y  # score every point of the grid, using all the data points final <- data.frame(X1 = as.vector(xx), X2 = as.vector(yy)) predicted <- knn_score(make_moons[, c("X1", "X2")], final, make_moons$y, k = 15) Z <- matrix(predicted, nrow(xx), ncol(xx))  go_figure() |>   add_contour(x = xrange, y = yrange, z = Z, colorscale = "RdBu") library(plotly.core) library(pracma) library(class)  make_moons <- read.csv(file = "data/make_moons.csv") make_moons$y <- as.character(make_moons$y) set.seed(123) train_index <- sample(nrow(make_moons), 3/4 * nrow(make_moons)) make_moons$split <- "Test Split Label" make_moons$split[train_index] <- "Train Split Label" make_moons$label <- paste(make_moons$split, make_moons$y)  # kNN score: the fraction of the k nearest training samples labelled "1" knn_score <- function(train, test, labels, k = 15) {   pred <- knn(train, test, labels, k = k, prob = TRUE)   ifelse(pred == "1", attr(pred, "prob"), 1 - attr(pred, "prob")) }  mesh_size <- .02 margin <- 0.25 x_min <- min(make_moons$X1) - margin x_max <- max(make_moons$X1) + margin y_min <- min(make_moons$X2) - margin y_max <- max(make_moons$X2) + margin xrange <- seq(x_min, x_max, mesh_size) yrange <- seq(y_min, y_max, mesh_size) xy <- meshgrid(x = xrange, y = yrange) xx <- xy$X yy <- xy$Y  # score every point of the grid, using all the data points final <- data.frame(X1 = as.vector(xx), X2 = as.vector(yy)) predicted <- knn_score(make_moons[, c("X1", "X2")], final, make_moons$y, k = 15) Z <- matrix(predicted, nrow(xx), ncol(xx))  symbols <- c(   "Train Split Label 0" = "square",   "Train Split Label 1" = "circle",   "Test Split Label 0" = "square-dot",   "Test Split Label 1" = "circle-dot" )  fig <- go_figure() |>   add_contour(x = xrange, y = yrange, z = Z, colorscale = "RdBu", opacity = 0.5) for (lab in names(symbols)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       data = make_moons[make_moons$label == lab, ],       x = ~X1,       y = ~X2,       mode = "markers",       name = lab,       marker = go_scatter_marker(         symbol = symbols[[lab]],         size = 12,         color = "lightyellow",         line = go_scatter_marker_line(color = "black", width = 1)       )     ) }  fig

text: also possible visualize prediction confidence model using heatmaps. example, can see compute confident model prediction every point 2D grid. , define confidence difference highest score sum score classes, certain point. Since scores add 1, 2 * max_score - 1, max_score proportion neighbours voted predicted class.
code: library(pracma) library(plotly.core) library(class)  data(iris) # We will use the iris data, which is included in R by default  mesh_size <- .02 margin <- 1  set.seed(123) train_index <- sample(nrow(iris), 3/4 * nrow(iris)) train_data <- iris[train_index, ] test_data <- iris[-train_index, ]  # Create a mesh grid on which we will run our model l_min <- min(iris$Sepal.Length) - margin l_max <- max(iris$Sepal.Length) + margin w_min <- min(iris$Sepal.Width) - margin w_max <- max(iris$Sepal.Width) + margin lrange <- seq(l_min, l_max, mesh_size) wrange <- seq(w_min, w_max, mesh_size)  mg <- meshgrid(lrange, wrange) ll <- mg$X ww <- mg$Y  # Run the classifier on the grid final <- data.frame(Sepal.Length = as.vector(ll), Sepal.Width = as.vector(ww)) pred <- knn(   train_data[, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width")],   final,   train_data$Species,   k = 15,   prob = TRUE )  # Compute the classifier confidence max_score <- matrix(attr(pred, "prob"), nrow(ll), ncol(ll)) diff <- 2 * max_score - 1  # Overlay the heatmap of the confidence on the scatter plot of the examples species_symbols <- c(setosa = "square-dot", versicolor = "circle-dot", virginica = "diamond")  fig <- go_figure() for (sp in names(species_symbols)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       data = test_data[test_data$Species == sp, ],       x = ~Sepal.Length,       y = ~Sepal.Width,       mode = "markers",       name = sp,       marker = go_scatter_marker(         symbol = species_symbols[[sp]],         size = 12,         color = "lightyellow",         line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 1.5)       )     ) } fig <- fig |>   add_heatmap(x = lrange, y = wrange, z = diff) |>   update_layout(title = "Prediction Confidence on Test Split")  fig

title: Map Configuration and Styling
text: Plotly supports two different kinds maps: Tile maps tile-based maps drawn MapLibre. figure created one add_scattermap(), add_choroplethmap() add_densitymap() traces, map layout object (go_map()) figure contains configuration information map . Geo maps outline-based maps. figure created add_scattergeo() add_choropleth(), geo layout object (go_geo()) figure contains configuration information map . page documents Geo outline-based maps, Map Layers documentation describes configure tile-based maps. Note: Every configuration option equally applicable non-empty maps created add_scattergeo() add_choropleth().

title: Map Configuration and Styling

Various lines area fills can shown hidden, color line-widths specified. default template, map frame physical features coastal outline filled land areas shown, small-scale 1:110m resolution: map physical features enabled styled, larger-scale 1:50m resolution:

title: Map Configuration and Styling
text: Geo maps drawn according given map projection flattens Earth’s roughly-spherical surface 2-dimensional space. available projections 'equirectangular', 'mercator', 'orthographic', 'natural earth', 'kavrayskiy7', 'miller', 'robinson', 'eckert4', 'azimuthal equal area', 'azimuthal equidistant', 'conic equal area', 'conic conformal', 'conic equidistant', 'gnomonic', 'stereographic', 'mollweide', 'hammer', 'transverse mercator', 'albers usa', 'winkel tripel', 'aitoff' 'sinusoidal'. Map projections can rotated using rotation go_geo_projection(), maps can translated using center go_geo(), well truncated certain longitude latitude range using range go_geo_lataxis() go_geo_lonaxis(). map uses attributes demonstrate types effect can yield:
code: library(plotly.core)  g <- go_geo(   projection = go_geo_projection(     type = "orthographic"   ),   showland = TRUE,   landcolor = "#e5ecf6" )  go_figure() |>   add_scattergeo(mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(geo = g) library(plotly.core)  g <- go_geo(   projection = go_geo_projection(     type = "natural earth"   ),   showland = TRUE,   landcolor = "#e5ecf6" )  go_figure() |>   add_scattergeo(mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(geo = g) library(plotly.core)  g <- go_geo(   projection = go_geo_projection(     rotation = go_geo_projection_rotation(lon = 30, lat = 30, roll = 30)   ),   center = go_geo_center(lon = -30, lat = -30),   lonaxis = go_geo_lonaxis(range = c(0, 200)),   lataxis = go_geo_lataxis(range = c(-50, 20)),   showland = TRUE,   landcolor = "#e5ecf6" )  go_figure() |>   add_scattergeo(mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(geo = g)

title: Map Subplots And Small Multiples
code:
library(plotly.core) library(dplyr) df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/1962_2006_walmart_store_openings.csv") years <- sort(unique(df$YEAR)) n_rows <- 9 n_cols <- ceiling(length(years) / n_rows) # one geo subplot per year; cells after the last year stay empty specs <- lapply(seq_len(n_rows), function(row) { lapply(seq_len(n_cols), function(col) { if ((row - 1) * n_cols + col <= length(years)) list(type = "geo") else NULL }) }) fig <- make_subplots( rows = n_rows, cols = n_cols, specs = specs, horizontal_spacing = 0.01, vertical_spacing = 0.01 ) for (idx in seq_along(years)) { yr <- years[[idx]] row <- (idx - 1) %/% n_cols + 1 col <- (idx - 1) %% n_cols + 1 fig <- fig |> add_scattergeo( data = filter(df, YEAR == yr), lon = ~LON, lat = ~LAT, mode = "markers", marker = go_scattergeo_marker(color = "blue", opacity = 0.5), row = row, col = col ) |> add_scattergeo( lon = -78, lat = 47, text = as.character(yr), mode = "text", textfont = go_font(color = "black"), row = row, col = col ) } # common map properties fig <- fig |> update_geos( scope = "usa", showland = TRUE, landcolor = "rgb(229, 229, 229)", showcountries = FALSE, subunitcolor = "white" ) |> update_layout( showlegend = FALSE, title = 'New Walmart Stores per year 1962-2006
Source: University of Minnesota', width = 1000, height = 900, hovermode = FALSE ) fig

what: How Layers Work in Tile Maps
title: Mapbox Layers
text: plotly.js longer uses Mapbox: scattermapbox, choroplethmapbox densitymapbox traces layout.mapbox replaced MapLibre-based scattermap, choroplethmap densitymap traces (add_scattermap(), add_choroplethmap(), add_densitymap()) layout.map (go_map()). figure contains one traces, layout figure contains configuration information map . map composed layers three different types. layout.map.style defines lowest layers, also known “base map” traces added add_scattermap() friends default rendered base map (can controlled via use attribute). layout.map.layers attribute accepts array go_map_layer() objects default rendered traces (can controlled via attribute).

title: Mapbox Layers
text: MapLibre need Mapbox Access Token. built-values layout.map.style work without one: white-bg yields empty white canvas results external HTTP requests open-street-map, carto-positron, carto-darkmatter, carto-voyager (-nolabels variants), basic, streets, outdoors, light, dark, satellite satellite-streets yield maps composed tiles various public tile servers require signups access tokens layout.map.style can also style URL style object defined MapLibre style spec.

what: Using layout.map.layers to Specify a Base Map
title: Mapbox Layers
text: access private tile servers, wish use tile server included list , recommended approach first set layout.map.style "white-bg" set layout.map.layers specify custom base map. omit setting layout.map.layers , using approach, data likely hidden fully-opaque raster tiles!

text: section, show apply simple regression model predicting tips server receive based various client attributes (sex, time week, whether smoker). using Linear Regression, simple model fits intercept (mean tip received server), adds slope feature use, value total bill.

title: ML Regression
code: library(reshape2) # to load tips data library(plotly.core) data(tips)  X <- tips$total_bill  lm_model <- lm(tip ~ total_bill, data = tips)  xy <- data.frame(total_bill = seq(min(X), max(X), length.out = 100)) xy$tip <- predict(lm_model, xy)  go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     data = tips,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~tip,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(opacity = 0.65),     name = "Tips"   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = xy,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~tip,     mode = "lines",     name = "Regression Fit"   )

title: ML Regression
text: one add_scatter() trace per data split, can easily color plot based predefined data split. coloring training testing data points different colors, can easily see model generalizes well test data .
code: library(reshape2) library(plotly.core) data(tips)  X <- tips$total_bill  set.seed(123) train_rows <- sample(nrow(tips), round(0.75 * nrow(tips))) tips_training <- tips[train_rows, ] tips_test <- tips[-train_rows, ]  lm_model <- lm(tip ~ total_bill, data = tips_training)  xy <- data.frame(total_bill = seq(min(X), max(X), length.out = 100)) xy$tip <- predict(lm_model, xy)  go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     data = tips_training,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~tip,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(opacity = 0.65),     name = "train"   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = tips_test,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~tip,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(opacity = 0.65),     name = "test"   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = xy,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~tip,     mode = "lines",     name = "prediction"   )

title: ML Regression
text: addition linear regression, ’s possible fit data using k-Nearest Neighbors. perform prediction new sample, model either takes weighted un-weighted average neighbors. order see difference two averaging options, train kNN model parameters, plot way previous graph. Notice can combine scatter points lines using Plotly. can learn multiple chart types.
code: library(reshape2) library(plotly.core) data(tips)  X <- tips$total_bill  # k-nearest-neighbors regression on one feature: the (optionally # inverse-distance weighted) mean of the k nearest training responses knn_predict <- function(x_train, y_train, x_new, k = 10, weighted = FALSE) {   vapply(x_new, function(x0) {     d <- abs(x_train - x0)     idx <- order(d)[seq_len(k)]     w <- if (weighted) 1 / pmax(d[idx], 1e-8) else rep(1, k)     sum(w * y_train[idx]) / sum(w)   }, numeric(1)) }  xy <- data.frame(total_bill = seq(min(X), max(X), length.out = 100)) # Model #1 xy$dist <- knn_predict(tips$total_bill, tips$tip, xy$total_bill, weighted = TRUE) # Model #2 xy$uni <- knn_predict(tips$total_bill, tips$tip, xy$total_bill, weighted = FALSE)  sex_colors <- c(Female = "#FF7F50", Male = "#6495ED")  tips |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~tip,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(       color = ~sex_colors[as.character(sex)],       opacity = 0.65     ),     split = ~sex   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = xy,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~dist,     name = "Weights: Distance",     mode = "lines"   ) |>   add_scatter(     data = xy,     x = ~total_bill,     y = ~uni,     name = "Weights: Uniform",     mode = "lines"   )

title: ML Regression
text: Visualize decision plane model whenever one variable input data. , use support vector machine radial basis function kernel (e1071::svm()) regression mode. generating 2D mesh surface, use pracma package.
code: library(plotly.core) library(e1071) library(pracma) # For meshgrid() data(iris)  mesh_size <- .02 margin <- 0 X <- iris[, c("Sepal.Width", "Sepal.Length")]  model <- svm(   Petal.Width ~ Sepal.Width + Sepal.Length,   data = iris,   type = "eps-regression",   kernel = "radial",   cost = 1.0 )  x_min <- min(X$Sepal.Width) - margin x_max <- max(X$Sepal.Width) - margin y_min <- min(X$Sepal.Length) - margin y_max <- max(X$Sepal.Length) - margin xrange <- seq(x_min, x_max, mesh_size) yrange <- seq(y_min, y_max, mesh_size) xy <- meshgrid(x = xrange, y = yrange) xx <- xy$X yy <- xy$Y dim_val <- dim(xx) final <- data.frame(Sepal.Width = c(xx), Sepal.Length = c(yy)) pred <- predict(model, final) pred <- matrix(pred, dim_val[1], dim_val[2])  iris |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter3d(     x = ~Sepal.Width,     y = ~Sepal.Length,     z = ~Petal.Width,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter3d_marker(size = 5)   ) |>   add_surface(     x = xrange,     y = yrange,     z = pred,     opacity = 0.65,     name = "pred_surface"   )

title: Multiple Axes
text: Use make_subplots() specs request secondary y axis cell, add traces secondary_y = TRUE.
code: library(plotly.core)  cell <- list(secondary_y = TRUE)  fig <- make_subplots(   rows = 2,   cols = 2,   specs = list(list(cell, cell), list(cell, cell)),   horizontal_spacing = 0.1,   vertical_spacing = 0.1 )  n <- 1 for (row in 1:2) {   for (col in 1:2) {     fig <- fig |>       add_scatter(         x = c(1, 2, 3),         y = c(2, 52, 62),         mode = "lines+markers",         name = paste0("yaxis", if (n == 1) "" else n, " data"),         row = row,         col = col       ) |>       add_scatter(         x = c(1, 2, 3),         y = c(40, 50, 60),         mode = "lines+markers",         name = paste0("yaxis", n + 1, " data"),         row = row,         col = col,         secondary_y = TRUE       )     n <- n + 2   } }  fig <- fig |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "#ffff", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "ffff") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "#ffff", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "ffff") |>   update_layout(     legend = go_legend(x = 1.05, y = 1),     plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6"   )  fig

title: PCA Visualization
text: dimensionality reduction technique using called Principal Component Analysis (PCA). powerful technique arises linear algebra probability theory. essence, computes matrix represents variation data (covariance matrix/eigenvectors), rank relevance (explained variance/eigenvalues).

title: PCA Visualization
text: First, let’s plot features see species Iris dataset grouped. Scatter Plot Matrix (splom), subplot displays feature another, NN features N×NN \times N matrix. example, plotting 4 features Iris dataset, thus can see sepal_width compared sepal_length, petal_width, forth. Keep mind pairs features can easily separate different species.
code: library(plotly.core)  data(iris)  axis_x <- go_xaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4,   title = go_xaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13)) ) axis_y <- go_yaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4,   title = go_yaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13)) )  iris |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = c("#636EFA", "#EF553B", "#00CC96")) |>   add_splom(     dimensions = list(       go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal length", values = ~Sepal.Length),       go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal width", values = ~Sepal.Width),       go_splom_dimension(label = "petal length", values = ~Petal.Length),       go_splom_dimension(label = "petal width", values = ~Petal.Width)     ),     diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE),     marker = go_splom_marker(       color = ~Species,       size = 7,       line = go_splom_marker_line(width = 1, color = "rgb(230,230,230)")     )   ) |>   update_layout(     hovermode = "closest",     dragmode = "select",     plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240, 0.95)",     xaxis = axis_x,     xaxis2 = axis_x,     xaxis3 = axis_x,     xaxis4 = axis_x,     yaxis = axis_y,     yaxis2 = axis_y,     yaxis3 = axis_y,     yaxis4 = axis_y   )

title: PCA Visualization
text: Now, apply PCA dataset, retrieve components. use splom trace display results, time features resulting principal components, ordered much variance able explain. importance explained variance demonstrated example . subplot PC3 PC4 clearly unable separate class, whereas subplot PC1 PC2 shows clear separation species.
code: library(plotly.core) library(stats) data(iris) X <- subset(iris, select = -c(Species)) prin_comp <- prcomp(X) explained_variance_ratio <- summary(prin_comp)[["importance"]]["Proportion of Variance", ] explained_variance_ratio <- 100 * explained_variance_ratio components <- prin_comp[["x"]] components <- data.frame(components) components <- cbind(components, iris$Species) components$PC3 <- -components$PC3 components$PC2 <- -components$PC2  axis_x <- go_xaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4,   title = go_xaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13)) ) axis_y <- go_yaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4,   title = go_yaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13)) )  pc_label <- function(i) {   paste("PC ", i, " (", toString(round(explained_variance_ratio[i], 1)), "%)", sep = "") } components |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = c("#636EFA", "#EF553B", "#00CC96")) |>   add_splom(     dimensions = list(       go_splom_dimension(label = pc_label(1), values = ~PC1),       go_splom_dimension(label = pc_label(2), values = ~PC2),       go_splom_dimension(label = pc_label(3), values = ~PC3),       go_splom_dimension(label = pc_label(4), values = ~PC4)     ),     diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE),     marker = go_splom_marker(color = ~iris$Species)   ) |>   update_layout(     legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "color")),     hovermode = "closest",     dragmode = "select",     plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240, 0.95)",     xaxis = axis_x,     xaxis2 = axis_x,     xaxis3 = axis_x,     xaxis4 = axis_x,     yaxis = axis_y,     yaxis2 = axis_y,     yaxis3 = axis_y,     yaxis4 = axis_y   )

title: PCA Visualization
text: many features visualize, might interested visualizing relevant components. components often capture majority explained variance, good way tell components sufficient modelling dataset. example , dataset contains 10 features, select first 4 components, since explain 99% total variance.
code: library(plotly.core) library(stats) library(MASS)  db <- Boston  prin_comp <- prcomp(db, rank. = 4)  components <- prin_comp[["x"]] components <- data.frame(components) components <- cbind(components, db$medv) components$PC2 <- -components$PC2 colnames(components)[5] <- "Median_Price"  tot_explained_variance_ratio <- summary(prin_comp)[["importance"]]["Proportion of Variance", ] tot_explained_variance_ratio <- 100 * sum(tot_explained_variance_ratio)  tit <- "Total Explained Variance = 99.56"  axis_x <- go_xaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4,   title = go_xaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13)) ) axis_y <- go_yaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4,   title = go_yaxis_title(font = go_font(size = 13)) )  components |>   go_figure() |>   add_splom(     dimensions = list(       go_splom_dimension(label = "PC1", values = ~PC1),       go_splom_dimension(label = "PC2", values = ~PC2),       go_splom_dimension(label = "PC3", values = ~PC3),       go_splom_dimension(label = "PC4", values = ~PC4)     ),     diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE),     marker = go_splom_marker(       color = ~Median_Price,       colorscale = "Viridis",       showscale = TRUE,       size = 7     )   ) |>   update_layout(     title = tit,     hovermode = "closest",     dragmode = "select",     plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240, 0.95)",     xaxis = axis_x,     xaxis2 = axis_x,     xaxis3 = axis_x,     xaxis4 = axis_x,     yaxis = axis_y,     yaxis2 = axis_y,     yaxis3 = axis_y,     yaxis4 = axis_y   )

title: PCA Visualization
text: Often, might interested seeing much variance PCA able explain increase number components, order decide many dimensions ultimately keep analyze. example shows quickly plot cumulative sum explained variance high-dimensional dataset like PimaIndiansDiabetes (read CSV copy). higher explained variance, able capture variability dataset, potentially lead better performance training model. mathematical explanation, see Q&thread.
code: library(plotly.core) library(stats)  # the Pima Indians Diabetes dataset (as in mlbench::PimaIndiansDiabetes) pima <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/diabetes.csv")  X <- subset(pima, select = -c(Outcome)) prin_comp <- prcomp(X) explained_variance_ratio <- summary(prin_comp)[["importance"]]["Proportion of Variance", ] cumsum <- cumsum(explained_variance_ratio) data <- data.frame(cumsum, seq(1, length(cumsum), 1)) colnames(data) <- c("Explained_Variance", "Components")  data |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     x = ~Components,     y = ~Explained_Variance,     mode = "lines",     fill = "tozeroy"   ) |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "# Components", tickvals = seq(1, length(cumsum), 1)),     yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Explained Variance")   )

title: PCA Visualization
text: also possible visualize loadings using shapes, use annotations indicate feature certain loading original belong . , define loadings : loadings=eigenvectors⋅eigenvalues loadings = eigenvectors \cdot \sqrt{eigenvalues} details linear algebra behind eigenvectors loadings, see Q&thread.
code: library(plotly.core) library(stats) data(iris) X <- subset(iris, select = -c(Species)) prin_comp <- prcomp(X, rank = 2) components <- prin_comp[["x"]] components <- data.frame(components) components <- cbind(components, iris$Species) components$PC2 <- -components$PC2 explained_variance <- summary(prin_comp)[["sdev"]] explained_variance <- explained_variance[1:2] comp <- prin_comp[["rotation"]] comp[, "PC2"] <- -comp[, "PC2"] loadings <- comp for (i in seq(explained_variance)) {   loadings[, i] <- comp[, i] * explained_variance[i] }  features <- c("sepal_length", "sepal_width", "petal_length", "petal_width")  components |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = c("#636EFA", "#EF553B", "#00CC96")) |>   add_scatter(     x = ~PC1,     y = ~PC2,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(color = ~iris$Species)   ) |>   update_layout(     legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "color")),     plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6",     xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "0"),     yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "1")   ) |>   add_shape(     type = "line",     x0 = 0,     y0 = 0,     x1 = loadings[, 1],     y1 = loadings[, 2],     line = go_shape_line(color = "black")   ) |>   add_annotation(     x = loadings[, 1],     y = loadings[, 2],     ax = 0,     ay = 0,     text = features,     xanchor = "center",     yanchor = "bottom"   )

what: ROC and PR Curves in R
title: ROC and PR Curves
text: Interpret results classification using Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) Precision-Recall (PR) Curves R Plotly.

title: ROC and PR Curves
text: diving receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, look two plots give context thresholds mechanism behind ROC PR curves. histogram, observe score spread positive labels binned near 1, lot negative labels close 0. set threshold score, bins left classified 0’s, everything right 1’s. obviously outliers, negative samples model gave high score, positive samples low score. set threshold right middle, outliers respectively become false positives false negatives. adjust thresholds, number false positives increase decrease, time number true positives also change; shown second plot. can see, model seems perform fairly well, true positive rate false positive rate decreases sharply increase threshold. two lines represent dimension ROC curve.
code: library(plotly.core) set.seed(0) X <- matrix(rnorm(10000), nrow = 500) y <- sample(0:1, 500, replace = TRUE) data <- data.frame(X, y) data$y <- as.factor(data$y) X <- subset(data, select = -c(y)) # Fit a logistic regression model logistic_glm <- glm(y ~ ., data = data, family = binomial) y_score <- predict(logistic_glm, X, type = "response") # ROC and PR curves computed with base R roc_df <- function(truth, score) { thr <- c(Inf, sort(unique(score), decreasing = TRUE), -Inf) data.frame( threshold = thr, tpr = sapply(thr, function(t) mean(score[truth == 1] >= t)), fpr = sapply(thr, function(t) mean(score[truth == 0] >= t)) ) } auc <- function(roc) { sum(diff(roc$fpr) * (head(roc$tpr, -1) + tail(roc$tpr, -1)) / 2) } z <- roc_df(data$y, y_score) fig1 <- data.frame(score = y_score, y = data$y) |> go_figure() |> update_layout(colorway = c("blue", "red")) |> add_histogram( x = ~score, opacity = 0.5, nbinsx = 50, marker = go_histogram_marker(color = ~y) ) |> update_layout(barmode = "overlay") fig1 fig2 <- z |> go_figure() |> add_scatter(x = ~threshold, y = ~fpr, mode = "lines", name = "False Positive Rate") |> add_scatter(x = ~threshold, y = ~tpr, mode = "lines", name = "True Positive Rate") |> update_layout( title = "TPR and FPR at every threshold", legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = " Rate ")) ) fig2

title: ROC and PR Curves
text: 2 classes, need plot ROC curve class separately. Make sure use one-versus-rest model, make sure problem multi-label format; otherwise, ROC curve might return expected results. example, use average precision metric, alternative scoring method area PR curve.
code: library(plotly.core)  # Artificially add noise to make task harder data(iris) ind <- sample.int(150, 50) samples <- sample(x = iris$Species, size = 50) iris[ind, "Species"] <- samples  # Define the inputs and outputs X <- subset(iris, select = -c(Species)) iris$Species <- as.factor(iris$Species)  # Fit a multinomial logistic regression model logistic <- nnet::multinom(Species ~ ., data = iris, trace = FALSE)  y_scores <- predict(logistic, X, type = "probs")  # One hot encode the labels in order to plot them y_onehot <- sapply(levels(iris$Species), function(l) as.integer(iris$Species == l))  # ROC and PR curves computed with base R roc_df <- function(truth, score) {   thr <- c(Inf, sort(unique(score), decreasing = TRUE), -Inf)   data.frame(     threshold = thr,     tpr = sapply(thr, function(t) mean(score[truth == 1] >= t)),     fpr = sapply(thr, function(t) mean(score[truth == 0] >= t))   ) } auc <- function(roc) {   sum(diff(roc$fpr) * (head(roc$tpr, -1) + tail(roc$tpr, -1)) / 2) }  # Create an empty figure, and iteratively add a line for each class fig <- go_figure() |>   add_shape(     type = "line",     x0 = 0,     x1 = 1,     y0 = 0,     y1 = 1,     line = go_shape_line(dash = "dash", color = "black")   ) for (cl in colnames(y_onehot)) {   roc <- roc_df(y_onehot[, cl], y_scores[, cl])   name <- paste0(cl, " (AUC=", round(auc(roc), 2), ")")   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(data = roc, x = ~fpr, y = ~tpr, mode = "lines", name = name) } fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "False Positive Rate"),     yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "True Positive Rate"),     legend = go_legend(x = 100, y = 0.5)   ) fig library(plotly.core)  # Artificially add noise to make task harder data(iris) ind <- sample.int(150, 50) samples <- sample(x = iris$Species, size = 50) iris[ind, "Species"] <- samples  # Define the inputs and outputs X <- subset(iris, select = -c(Species)) iris$Species <- as.factor(iris$Species)  # Fit a multinomial logistic regression model logistic <- nnet::multinom(Species ~ ., data = iris, trace = FALSE)  y_scores <- predict(logistic, X, type = "probs")  # One hot encode the labels in order to plot them y_onehot <- sapply(levels(iris$Species), function(l) as.integer(iris$Species == l))  # precision-recall curve and average precision computed with base R pr_df <- function(truth, score) {   thr <- sort(unique(score), decreasing = TRUE)   tp <- sapply(thr, function(t) sum(score >= t & truth == 1))   fp <- sapply(thr, function(t) sum(score >= t & truth == 0))   data.frame(     threshold = c(Inf, thr),     recall = c(0, tp / sum(truth == 1)),     precision = c(1, tp / (tp + fp))   ) } avg_precision <- function(pr) {   sum(diff(pr$recall) * pr$precision[-1]) }  # Create an empty figure, and add a new line for each class fig <- go_figure() |>   add_shape(     type = "line",     x0 = 0,     x1 = 1,     y0 = 1,     y1 = 0,     line = go_shape_line(dash = "dash", color = "black")   ) for (cl in colnames(y_onehot)) {   pr <- pr_df(y_onehot[, cl], y_scores[, cl])   name <- paste0(cl, " (AP = ", round(avg_precision(pr), 2), ")")   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(data = pr, x = ~recall, y = ~precision, mode = "lines", name = name) } fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Recall"),     yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Precision"),     legend = go_legend(x = 100, y = 0.5)   ) fig

code: library(plotly.core) library(dplyr)  # airport locations air <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2011_february_us_airport_traffic.csv")  # flights between airports flights <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/2011_february_aa_flight_paths.csv") flights$id <- seq_len(nrow(flights))  # one segment per flight, separated by NA seg_lon <- as.vector(rbind(flights$start_lon, flights$end_lon, NA)) seg_lat <- as.vector(rbind(flights$start_lat, flights$end_lat, NA))  go_figure() |>   add_scattermap(     data = air,     lon = ~long,     lat = ~lat,     mode = "markers",     text = ~airport,     marker = go_scattermap_marker(       color = "red",       size = ~scales::rescale(sqrt(cnt), to = c(3, 20)),       opacity = 0.5     ),     hoverinfo = "text"   ) |>   add_scattermap(     lon = seg_lon,     lat = seg_lat,     mode = "lines",     opacity = 0.3,     line = go_scattermap_line(width = 1, color = "red"),     hoverinfo = "none"   ) |>   update_layout(     plot_bgcolor = "#191A1A",     paper_bgcolor = "#191A1A",     map = go_map(       style = "carto-darkmatter",       zoom = 1.5,       center = go_map_center(lat = median(air$lat), lon = median(air$long))     ),     margin = go_margin(l = 0, r = 0, b = 0, t = 0, pad = 0),     showlegend = FALSE   )

title: Sliders
code: library(plotly.core)  df <- data.frame(   x = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),   y = c("1", "1", "1", "1", "1") )  # create steps for slider steps <- list(   go_slider_step(     args = list("marker.color", "red"),     label = "Red",     method = "restyle",     value = "1"   ),   go_slider_step(     args = list("marker.color", "green"),     label = "Green",     method = "restyle",     value = "2"   ),   go_slider_step(     args = list("marker.color", "blue"),     label = "Blue",     method = "restyle",     value = "3"   ) )  df |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     x = ~x,     y = ~y,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(size = 20, color = "green")   ) |>   update_layout(     title = "Basic Slider",     sliders = list(       go_slider(         active = 1,         currentvalue = go_slider_currentvalue(prefix = "Color: "),         pad = go_slider_pad(t = 60),         steps = steps       )     )   )

title: Sliders
code: library(plotly.core)  x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 1000)  # create data aval <- list() for (step in 1:11) {   aval[[step]] <- list(     visible = FALSE,     name = paste0("v = ", step),     x = x,     y = sin(step * x)   ) } aval[[3]]$visible <- TRUE  # create steps and plot all traces steps <- list() fig <- go_figure() for (i in 1:11) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       x = aval[[i]]$x,       y = aval[[i]]$y,       visible = aval[[i]]$visible,       name = aval[[i]]$name,       mode = "lines",       hoverinfo = "name",       line = go_scatter_line(color = "#00CED1"),       showlegend = FALSE     )    visible <- rep(FALSE, length(aval))   visible[i] <- TRUE   steps[[i]] <- go_slider_step(args = list("visible", visible), method = "restyle") }  # add slider control to plot fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     sliders = list(       go_slider(         active = 3,         currentvalue = go_slider_currentvalue(prefix = "Frequency: "),         steps = steps       )     )   )  fig

title: Sliders
text: #Reference See go_slider() go_updatemenu() information options!
code: library(plotly.core)  df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/globe_contours.csv") df$id <- seq_len(nrow(df))  library(tidyr) d <- df %>%   gather(key, value, -id) %>%   separate(key, c("l", "line"), "\\.") %>%   spread(l, value)  geo <- go_geo(   showland = TRUE,   showlakes = TRUE,   showcountries = TRUE,   showocean = TRUE,   countrywidth = 0.5,   landcolor = "rgb(230, 145, 56)",   lakecolor = "rgb(0, 255, 255)",   oceancolor = "rgb(0, 255, 255)",   projection = go_geo_projection(     type = "orthographic",     rotation = go_geo_projection_rotation(lon = -100, lat = 40, roll = 0)   ),   lonaxis = go_geo_lonaxis(     showgrid = TRUE,     gridcolor = "rgb(102,102,102)",     gridwidth = 0.5   ),   lataxis = go_geo_lataxis(     showgrid = TRUE,     gridcolor = "rgb(102,102,102)",     gridwidth = 0.5   ) )  ## add custom events  # dropdown projections <- data.frame(type = c("equirectangular", "mercator", "orthographic", "natural earth","kavrayskiy7",                                    "miller", "robinson", "eckert4", "azimuthal equal area","azimuthal equidistant",                                    "conic equal area", "conic conformal", "conic equidistant", "gnomonic", "stereographic",                                    "mollweide", "hammer", "transverse mercator", "albers usa", "winkel tripel"))  all_buttons <- lapply(projections$type, function(type) {   go_updatemenu_button(     method = "relayout",     args = list(list(geo.projection.type = type)),     label = type   ) })  # sliders lon_range <- seq(-180, 180, 10) lat_range <- seq(-90, 90, 10)  all_lat <- lapply(lat_range, function(lat) {   go_slider_step(     method = "relayout",     args = list(list(geo.projection.rotation.lat = lat)),     label = lat   ) })  all_lon <- lapply(lon_range, function(lon) {   go_slider_step(     method = "relayout",     args = list(list(geo.projection.rotation.lon = lon)),     label = lon   ) })  # annotations annot <- go_annotation(   x = 0,   y = 0.8,   text = "Projection",   yanchor = "bottom",   xref = "paper",   xanchor = "right",   showarrow = FALSE )  # original d3-globe with contours, one red shade per line lines <- unique(d$line) reds <- colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Reds"))(length(lines))  fig <- go_figure() for (i in seq_along(lines)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scattergeo(       data = d[d$line == lines[i], ],       lon = ~lon,       lat = ~lat,       mode = "lines",       line = go_scattergeo_line(color = reds[i]),       name = lines[i]     ) } fig <- fig |>   update_layout(showlegend = FALSE, geo = geo)  # plot with custom events fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     annotations = list(annot),     updatemenus = list(       go_updatemenu(active = 2, x = 0, y = 0.8, buttons = all_buttons)     ),     sliders = list(       go_slider(         active = (length(lon_range) - 1) / 2,         currentvalue = go_slider_currentvalue(prefix = "Longitude: "),         pad = go_slider_pad(t = 20),         steps = all_lon       ),       go_slider(         active = (length(lat_range) - 1) / 2,         currentvalue = go_slider_currentvalue(prefix = "Latitude: "),         pad = go_slider_pad(t = 100),         steps = all_lat       )     )   )  fig
