what: Splom of the Iris data set
title: Splom
text: Iris dataset contains four data variables, sepal length, sepal width, petal length petal width, 150 iris flowers. flowers labeled Iris-setosa, Iris-versicolor, Iris-virginica. Define discrete colorscale three colors corresponding three flower classes: create splom: scatter plots principal diagonal can removed setting diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE): plot lower/upper half splom switch default showlowerhalf = TRUE / showupperhalf = FALSE: dimension property, visible, set default TRUE. can choose remove variable splom, setting visible = FALSE corresponding dimension. case default grid associated scatterplot matrix keeps number cells, cells row column corresponding visible false dimension empty:
code: library(plotly.core)  df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/iris-data.csv") pl_colorscale <- list(   c(0.0, "#19d3f3"),   c(0.333, "#19d3f3"),   c(0.333, "#e763fa"),   c(0.666, "#e763fa"),   c(0.666, "#636efa"),   c(1, "#636efa") ) xaxis_style <- go_xaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4 ) yaxis_style <- go_yaxis(   showline = FALSE,   zeroline = FALSE,   gridcolor = "#ffff",   ticklen = 4 )  dims <- list(   go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal length", values = ~sepal.length),   go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal width", values = ~sepal.width),   go_splom_dimension(label = "petal length", values = ~petal.length),   go_splom_dimension(label = "petal width", values = ~petal.width) )  fig <- df |>   go_figure() |>   add_splom(     dimensions = dims,     text = ~class,     marker = go_splom_marker(       color = as.integer(factor(df$class)),       colorscale = pl_colorscale,       size = 7,       line = go_splom_marker_line(         width = 1,         color = "rgb(230,230,230)"       )     )   ) |>   update_layout(     title = "Iris Data set",     hovermode = "closest",     dragmode = "select",     plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240, 0.95)",     xaxis = xaxis_style,     yaxis = yaxis_style,     xaxis2 = xaxis_style,     xaxis3 = xaxis_style,     xaxis4 = xaxis_style,     yaxis2 = yaxis_style,     yaxis3 = yaxis_style,     yaxis4 = yaxis_style   )  fig library(plotly.core)  fig2 <- fig |>   update_traces(diagonal = go_splom_diagonal(visible = FALSE))  fig2 library(plotly.core)  fig2 <- fig |>   update_traces(showupperhalf = FALSE)  fig2 library(plotly.core)  dims[[3]] <- go_splom_dimension(   label = "petal length",   values = ~petal.length,   visible = FALSE ) fig2 <- fig |>   update_traces(dimensions = dims)  fig2

title: Exporting Graphs as Static Images
text: plotly.core R package, can export graphs create static images .png, .jpg/.jpeg, .webp, .eps, .svg, /.pdf formats using save_image() function, renders figure headless Chrome browser. Note: important aware R graphs containing WebGL-based traces (.e. type scattergl, contourgl, scatter3d, surface, mesh3d, scatterpolargl, cone, streamtube, splom, /parcoords) include encapsulated rasters instead vectors parts image exported static images vector format like .eps, .svg, /.pdf. Note Static image export runs entirely locally. network requests made Chart Studio web service invoke save_image() function export static images R session.

title: Exporting Graphs as Static Images
text: save_image() needs Chrome Chromium browser. uses installed Google Chrome (another Chromium-based browser) one; otherwise install_chrome() downloads Chrome Headless Shell plotly.core use. Python needed.

what: Export R Graphs As Static Images Using save_image()
title: Exporting Graphs as Static Images
text: save_image() function accepts two parameters. first figure exported second filename; format taken file extension. Optional width, height scale arguments control image size. example, running following commands R session export graph stored fig file called surface-plot.svg:
code: library(plotly.core)  fig <- go_figure() |>   add_surface(z = ~volcano) save_image(fig, "surface-plot.svg")

title: Styling Plotly Figures in R
text: Plotly’s R graphing library makes easy create interactive, publication-quality graphs. specifically, 2 ways can style customize figures made plotly.core: Control common parameters like titles, labeling colors arguments add_<trace>() functions Updating figure’s layout update_layout(), update_xaxes(), update_yaxes() friends

title: Styling Plotly Figures in R
text: Many common styling options can set directly adding traces updating layout: title (update_layout()) set figure title name set legend entry trace, title go_xaxis(), go_yaxis() go_legend() set axis legend titles. default, axes titled column names x y formulas. categoryorder categoryarray go_xaxis() override default category ordering behaviour, use levels factor, otherwise order data appears input. hovertemplate, hoverinfo axes’ hoverformat control attributes appear hover label formatted. Various color-related attributes marker = go_bar_marker(color = ...), colorscale, colorbar layout colorway set colors used figure. illustrate , simple, default figure made Plotly, one bar trace per payer gender. Note default orderings x-axis categories. figure, restyled adding extra parameters:
code: library(reshape2) library(plotly.core) data("tips") tips |> go_figure() |> add_bar(x = ~day, y = ~total_bill, marker = go_bar_marker(color = ~sex)) |> update_layout(barmode = "stack") library(reshape2) library(plotly.core) data("tips") sex_colors <- c(Female = "#3399FF", Male = "#FF6666") xform <- go_xaxis( title = "Day of Week", categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun") ) tips |> go_figure() |> update_layout(colorway = sex_colors) |> add_bar( x = ~day, y = ~total_bill, marker = go_bar_marker(color = ~sex) ) |> update_layout( barmode = "stack", xaxis = xform, yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Sum of Receipts"), title = "Receipts by Payer Gender and Day of Week", legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = " Payer Gender ")) )

what: Updating or Modifying Figures made with Plotly
title: Styling Plotly Figures in R
text: figure , additional customizations axes legend.
code: library(reshape2) library(plotly.core)  data("tips")  sex_colors <- c(Female = "#3399FF", Male = "#FF6666")  xform <- go_xaxis(   title = "Day of Week",   categoryorder = "array",   categoryarray = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun") )  fig <- tips |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = sex_colors) |>   add_bar(     x = ~day,     y = ~total_bill,     marker = go_bar_marker(color = ~sex)   ) # the y-axis prefix given as dollars fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     barmode = "stack",     xaxis = xform,     yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Sum of Receipts", tickprefix = "$"),     title = "Receipts by Payer Gender and Day of Week"   ) # customize legend orientation & position fig <- fig |>   update_layout(legend = go_legend(x = 0.2, y = 1, orientation = "h")) # add a horizontal "target" line fig <- fig |>   add_shape(     type = "line",     xref = "paper",     x0 = 0,     x1 = 1,     y0 = 950,     y1 = 950,     line = go_shape_line(dash = "dash", color = "black")   ) # add a text callout with arrow fig <- fig |>   add_annotation(     x = "Fri",     y = 400,     text = "Below Target !",     showarrow = TRUE,     arrowhead = 1,     ax = 20,     ay = -40   ) # customize font fig <- fig |>   update_layout(font = go_font(family = "Rockwell"))  fig

title: Subplots
text: Plotly’s R graphing library makes easy create interactive, publication-quality graphs. Plotly also subplot capabilities. page documents usage make_subplots() function.

title: Subplots
text: Figures subplots created using make_subplots() function, traces added given subplot row col arguments add_*(). example creating figure includes two scatter traces side--side since 2 columns 1 row subplot layout.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = 2) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(4, 5, 6),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(20, 30, 40),     y = c(50, 60, 70),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Side By Side Subplots")

title: Subplots
text: example creating figure subplots stacked top since 3 rows 1 column subplot layout.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(rows = 3, cols = 1) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(3, 4, 5),     y = c(1000, 1100, 1200),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(2, 3, 4),     y = c(100, 110, 120),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(0, 1, 2),     y = c(10, 11, 12),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 3,     col = 1   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Stacked Subplots") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

title: Subplots

code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(rows = 2, cols = 2) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(4, 5, 6),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(20, 30, 40),     y = c(50, 60, 70),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(300, 400, 500),     y = c(600, 700, 800),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(4000, 5000, 6000),     y = c(7000, 8000, 9000),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

title: Subplots
text: subplot_titles argument make_subplots() can used position text annotations titles subplot. example adding subplot titles 2 x 2 subplot grid scatter traces.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(   rows = 2,   cols = 2,   subplot_titles = c("Plot 1", "Plot 2", "Plot 3", "Plot 4") ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(4, 5, 6),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(20, 30, 40),     y = c(50, 60, 70),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(300, 400, 500),     y = c(600, 700, 800),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(4000, 5000, 6000),     y = c(7000, 8000, 9000),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Multiple Subplots with Titles") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

what: Customize Subplot Column Widths and Row Heights
title: Subplots
text: column_widths argument make_subplots() can used customize relative widths columns subplot grid. set vector numbers sum 1, used compute relative widths subplot grid columns. row_heights argument serves purpose controlling relative heights rows subplot grid. example creating figure two scatter traces side--side subplots. left subplot set wider right one.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = 2, column_widths = c(0.7, 0.3)) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(4, 5, 6),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(20, 30, 40),     y = c(50, 60, 70),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

title: Subplots
text: figure subplots created using make_subplots() function, axis properties (title, font, range, grid style, etc.) can customized using update_xaxes() update_yaxes() figure functions. default, functions apply x axes y axes figure. row col arguments can used control axes targeted update. example creates figure 2 x 2 subplot grid, populates subplot scatter trace, updates x y axis titles subplot individually.
code: library(plotly.core)  # initialize figure with subplots fig <- make_subplots(   rows = 2,   cols = 2,   subplot_titles = c("Plot 1", "Plot 2", "Plot 3", "Plot 4"),   horizontal_spacing = 0.1,   vertical_spacing = 0.15 ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(4, 5, 6),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(20, 30, 40),     y = c(50, 60, 70),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(300, 400, 500),     y = c(600, 700, 800),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(4000, 5000, 6000),     y = c(7000, 8000, 9000),     mode = "lines+markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Customizing Subplot Axes") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )  # update axis properties fig <- fig |>   update_xaxes(title = "xaxis1 title", row = 1, col = 1) |>   update_xaxes(title = "xaxis2 title", range = c(10, 50), row = 1, col = 2) |>   update_xaxes(title = "xaxis3 title", showgrid = FALSE, row = 2, col = 1) |>   update_xaxes(title = "xaxis4 title", type = "log", row = 2, col = 2) |>   update_yaxes(title = "yaxis1 title", row = 1, col = 1) |>   update_yaxes(title = "yaxis2 title", range = c(40, 80), row = 1, col = 2) |>   update_yaxes(title = "yaxis3 title", showgrid = FALSE, row = 2, col = 1) |>   update_yaxes(title = "yaxis4 title", row = 2, col = 2)  fig

title: Subplots
text: shared_xaxes argument make_subplots() can used link x axes subplots resulting figure. vertical_spacing argument used control vertical spacing rows subplot grid. example creates figure 3 vertically stacked subplots linked x axes. small vertical_spacing value used reduce spacing subplot rows.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(   rows = 3,   cols = 1,   shared_xaxes = TRUE,   vertical_spacing = 0.02 ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(3, 4, 5),     y = c(1000, 1100, 1200),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(2, 3, 4),     y = c(100, 110, 120),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(0, 1, 2),     y = c(10, 11, 12),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 3,     col = 1   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Stacked Subplots with Shared X-Axes") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

title: Subplots
text: shared_yaxes argument can used link y axes subplots resulting figure. example creates figure 2 x 2 subplot grid, y axes row linked.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(rows = 2, cols = 2, shared_yaxes = TRUE) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(2, 3, 4),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(20, 30, 40),     y = c(5, 5, 5),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(2, 3, 4),     y = c(600, 700, 800),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(4000, 5000, 6000),     y = c(7000, 8000, 9000),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 2,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Multiple Subplots with Shared Y-Axes") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

title: Subplots
text: share colorscale information multiple subplots, can use coloraxis (see go_coloraxis()).
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = 2, shared_yaxes = TRUE) |>   add_bar(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(4, 5, 6),     marker = go_bar_marker(color = c(4, 5, 6), coloraxis = "coloraxis"),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_bar(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(2, 3, 5),     marker = go_bar_marker(color = c(2, 3, 5), coloraxis = "coloraxis"),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(     showlegend = FALSE,     coloraxis = go_coloraxis(colorscale = "RdBu")   ) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

what: Custom Sized Subplot with Subplot Titles
title: Subplots
text: specs argument make_subplots() used custom size individual plots subplot: subplot can span several columns (colspan) rows (rowspan), NULL marks empty cell. example creates 2 2 subplot grid containing 3 subplots.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(   rows = 2,   cols = 2,   specs = list(     list(list(), list()),     list(list(colspan = 2), NULL)   ),   subplot_titles = c("First Subplot", "Second Subplot", "Third Subplot") ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2, 3),     y = c(2, 1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   update_layout(title = "Specs with Subplot Title", showlegend = FALSE) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

title: Subplots
text: example uses rowspan colspan subplot options create custom subplot layout subplots mixed sizes.
code: library(plotly.core)  make_subplots(   rows = 5,   cols = 2,   specs = list(     list(list(), list(rowspan = 2)),     list(list(), NULL),     list(list(rowspan = 2, colspan = 2), NULL),     list(NULL, NULL),     list(list(), list())   ),   print_grid = TRUE ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "(1,1)",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "(2,1)",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 2,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "(1,2)",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "(3,1)",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 3,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "(5,1)",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 5,     col = 1   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = c(1, 2),     y = c(1, 2),     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "(5,2)",     marker = go_scatter_marker(line = go_scatter_marker_line(width = 3)),     row = 5,     col = 2   ) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) ## This is the format of your plot grid: ## [ (1,1) x,y   ]  ⎡ (1,2) x2,y2 ⎤ ## [ (2,1) x3,y3 ]  ⎣      :      ⎦ ## ⎡ (3,1) x4,y4           -      ⎤ ## ⎣      :                :      ⎦ ## [ (5,1) x5,y5 ]  [ (5,2) x6,y6 ]

title: Subplots
text: default, make_subplots() function assumes traces added subplots 2-dimensional cartesian traces (e.g. scatter, bar, histogram, violin, etc.). subplot types (e.g. "scene", "polar", "domain") set type cell specs: trace type: trace type name (e.g. "bar", "contour", "pie", "scatter", etc.) used determine appropriate subplot type trace. example creates populates 2 x 2 subplot grid containing 4 different trace types.
code: library(plotly.core)  data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/school_earnings.csv") density <- density(ggplot2::diamonds$carat)  make_subplots(   rows = 2,   cols = 2,   horizontal_spacing = 0.1,   vertical_spacing = 0.1 ) |>   add_bar(y = c(2, 3, 1), row = 1, col = 1) |>   add_scatter(     data = data,     x = ~Women,     y = ~Men,     text = ~School,     mode = "markers",     marker = go_scatter_marker(       color = ~Gap,       colorscale = "Reds",       showscale = FALSE,       size = ~Gap,       opacity = 0.5     ),     row = 1,     col = 2   ) |>   add_contour(z = ~volcano, showscale = FALSE, row = 2, col = 1) |>   add_scatter(     x = density$x,     y = density$y,     mode = "lines",     fill = "tozeroy",     row = 2,     col = 2   ) |>   update_xaxes(showgrid = FALSE, row = 1, col = 2) |>   update_yaxes(showgrid = FALSE, row = 1, col = 2) |>   update_xaxes(title = "Carat", row = 2, col = 2) |>   update_yaxes(title = "Density", row = 2, col = 2) |>   update_layout(showlegend = FALSE) |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6") |>   update_xaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   ) |>   update_yaxes(     zerolinecolor = "#ffff",     zerolinewidth = 2,     gridcolor = "#ffff"   )

what: Controlling text orientation inside sunburst sectors
title: Sunburst Charts
text: insidetextorientation attribute controls orientation text inside sectors. “auto” texts may automatically rotated fit maximum size inside slice. Using “horizontal” (resp. “radial”, “tangential”) forces text horizontal (resp. radial tangential). Note plotly.js may reduce font size order fit text requested orientation.
code: library(plotly.core)  df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/718417069ead87650b90472464c7565dc8c2cb1c/coffee-flavors.csv")  df |>   go_figure() |>   add_sunburst(     ids = ~ids,     labels = ~labels,     parents = ~parents,     domain = go_domain(column = 1),     maxdepth = 2,     insidetextorientation = "radial"   )

title: Sunburst Charts
text: order create sunburst chart subplots, use domain attribute (see go_domain()) layout grid attribute (see go_grid()). #Reference See go_sunburst() information chart attribute options!
code: library(plotly.core)  d1 <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/coffee-flavors.csv") d2 <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/718417069ead87650b90472464c7565dc8c2cb1c/sunburst-coffee-flavors-complete.csv")  go_figure() |>   add_sunburst(     data = d1,     ids = ~ids,     labels = ~labels,     parents = ~parents,     maxdepth = 2,     domain = go_domain(column = 0)   ) |>   add_sunburst(     data = d2,     ids = ~ids,     labels = ~labels,     parents = ~parents,     maxdepth = 3,     domain = go_domain(column = 1)   ) |>   update_layout(     grid = go_grid(columns = 2, rows = 1),     margin = go_margin(l = 0, r = 0, b = 0, t = 0),     sunburstcolorway = c(       "#636efa", "#EF553B", "#00cc96", "#ab63fa", "#19d3f3",       "#e763fa", "#FECB52", "#FFA15A", "#FF6692", "#B6E880"     ),     extendsunburstcolors = TRUE   )

title: t-SNE and UMAP projections
text: First, let’s try visualize every feature Iris dataset, color everything species. use Scatter Plot Matrix (splom), lets us plot feature everything else, convenient dataset 3 dimensions. t-SNE UMAP projection examples original page need tsne umap packages available plotly.core yet. computed 2D 3D embedding, plot add_scatter() add_scatter3d(), one trace per class, shown scatter plot 3D scatter plot pages.
code: library(plotly.core) data(iris)  species_colors <- c(setosa = "#636EFA", versicolor = "#EF553B", virginica = "#00CC96")  # colouring by Species adds one trace per species, coloured from the colorway fig <- iris |>   go_figure() |>   update_layout(colorway = species_colors) |>   add_splom(     dimensions = list(       go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal_width", values = ~Sepal.Width),       go_splom_dimension(label = "sepal_length", values = ~Sepal.Length),       go_splom_dimension(label = "petal_width", values = ~Petal.Width),       go_splom_dimension(label = "petal_length", values = ~Petal.Length)     ),     marker = go_splom_marker(color = ~Species)   )  xaxis <- go_xaxis(showline = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, gridcolor = "#ffff", ticklen = 4) yaxis <- go_yaxis(showline = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, gridcolor = "#ffff", ticklen = 4)  fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "species")),     hovermode = "closest",     dragmode = "select",     plot_bgcolor = "rgba(240,240,240,0.95)",     xaxis = xaxis,     xaxis2 = xaxis,     xaxis3 = xaxis,     xaxis4 = xaxis,     yaxis = yaxis,     yaxis2 = yaxis,     yaxis3 = yaxis,     yaxis4 = yaxis   )  fig

title: Ternary Contour Plot
text: #Reference See go_scatterternary() information options!
code: library(plotly.core) library(jsonlite)  df <- fromJSON(   "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/davenquinn/988167471993bc2ece29/raw/f38d9cb3dd86e315e237fde5d65e185c39c931c2/data.json",   simplifyVector = FALSE )  colors <- c("#8dd3c7", "#ffffb3", "#bebada",             "#fb8072", "#80b1d3", "#fdb462",             "#b3de69", "#fccde5", "#d9d9d9",             "#bc80bd", "#ccebc5", "#ffed6f")  fig <- go_figure()  for (i in seq_along(df)) {   l <- sapply(df[[i]], function(pt) pt$clay)   m <- sapply(df[[i]], function(pt) pt$sand)   n <- sapply(df[[i]], function(pt) pt$silt)    fig <- fig |>     add_scatterternary(       a = l,       b = m,       c = n,       name = names(df)[i],       mode = "lines",       line = go_scatterternary_line(color = "#444"),       fill = "toself",       fillcolor = colors[i],       showlegend = FALSE     ) }  axis <- function(title) {   go_ternary_axis(     title = title,     ticksuffix = "%",     min = 0.01,     linewidth = 2,     ticks = "outside"   ) }  fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     title = "Simple Ternary Contour Plot in R",     ternary = go_ternary(       sum = 100,       aaxis = axis("clay"),       baxis = axis("sand"),       caxis = axis("silt")     )   )  fig

title: Ternary Plots
text: #Reference See go_scatterternary() information options!
code: library(plotly.core)  journalist <- c(75, 70, 75, 5, 10, 10, 20, 10, 15, 10, 20) developer <- c(25, 10, 20, 60, 80, 90, 70, 20, 5, 10, 10) designer <- c(0, 20, 5, 35, 10, 0, 10, 70, 80, 80, 70) label <- c("point 1", "point 2", "point 3", "point 4", "point 5", "point 6",            "point 7", "point 8", "point 9", "point 10", "point 11")  df <- data.frame(journalist, developer, designer, label)  # axis layout axis <- function(title) {   go_ternary_axis(     title = go_ternary_axis_title(text = title, font = go_font(size = 20)),     tickfont = go_font(size = 15),     tickcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",     ticklen = 5   ) }  df |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatterternary(     mode = "markers",     a = ~journalist,     b = ~developer,     c = ~designer,     text = ~label,     marker = go_scatterternary_marker(       symbol = 100,       color = "#DB7365",       size = 14,       line = go_scatterternary_marker_line(width = 2)     )   ) |>   update_layout(     title = "Simple Ternary Plot with Markers",     ternary = go_ternary(       sum = 100,       aaxis = axis("Journalist"),       baxis = axis("Developer"),       caxis = axis("Designer")     )   )

title: Text and Annotations
text: pie, bar, sunburst treemap traces, possible force text labels size thanks uniformtext layout parameter. minsize attribute sets font size, mode attribute sets happens labels fit desired fontsize: either hide show overflow.
code:
library(plotly.core) df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) df <- df[which(df$year == 2007 & df$continent == "Europe" & df$pop > 2.e6), ] df |> go_figure() |> add_bar( x = ~country, y = ~pop, text = ~lifeExp, name = "", hovertemplate = paste("%{x}", "
lifeExp: %{text:.2s}
"), texttemplate = "%{y:.2s}", textposition = "outside" ) |> update_layout(uniformtext = go_uniformtext(minsize = 8, mode = "hide")) library(plotly.core) df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) df <- df[which(df$year == 2007 & df$continent == "Asia"), ] df |> go_figure() |> add_pie(labels = ~country, values = ~pop, textposition = "inside") |> update_layout(uniformtext = go_uniformtext(minsize = 12, mode = "hide"))

what: Customize Displayed Text with a Text Template
title: Text and Annotations
text: show arbitrary text chart can use texttemplate (see e.g. go_pie()), template string used rendering information, override textinfo. template string can include variables %{variable} format, numbers d3-format’s syntax, date d3-time-fomrat’s syntax. texttemplate customizes text appears plot vs. hovertemplate customizes tooltip text.
code:
library(plotly.core) go_figure() |> add_pie( values = c(40000000, 20000000, 30000000, 10000000), labels = c("Wages", "Operating expenses", "Cost of sales", "Insurance"), texttemplate = "%{label}: %{value:$,s}
(%{percent})", textposition = "inside" )

(%{a:.2f}, %{b:.2f}, %{c:.2f})", textposition = "bottom center", textfont = go_font( family = "Times", size = c(18, 21, 20), color = c("IndianRed", "MediumPurple", "DarkOrange") ) )

what: Time Series using Axes of type date
title: Time Series and Date Axes
text: Time series can represented using cartesian trace (add_scatter(), add_bar() etc). examples charts, see documentation line scatter plots bar charts. financial applications, Plotly can also used create Candlestick charts OHLC charts, default date axes. Plotly doesn’t auto set data type axis date. give values using .Date() axis mention ’s data type date.
code: library(plotly.core)  # Weekly stock prices for 2018-2019, normalized to the first week stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/master/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz" stock <- data.table::fread(stocks_url, data.table = FALSE) stock$date <- as.Date(stock$date) names(stock)[names(stock) == "FB"] <- "META"  stock |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~date, y = ~GOOG, mode = "lines", name = "GOOG") |>   update_layout(showlegend = FALSE) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900) library(plotly.core)  stock <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv")  stock |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~Date, y = ~AAPL.High, mode = "lines") |>   update_layout(showlegend = FALSE) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900)

title: Time Series and Date Axes

code: library(plotly.core)  # Weekly stock prices for 2018-2019, normalized to the first week stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/master/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz" stock <- data.table::fread(stocks_url, data.table = FALSE) stock$date <- as.Date(stock$date) names(stock)[names(stock) == "FB"] <- "META"  stock |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~date, y = ~GOOG, mode = "lines", fill = "tozeroy", name = "GOOG") |>   update_layout(showlegend = FALSE, yaxis = go_yaxis(range = c(0.8, 1.25))) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900) library(plotly.core)  # Weekly stock prices for 2018-2019, normalized to the first week stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/master/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz" stock <- data.table::fread(stocks_url, data.table = FALSE) stock$date <- as.Date(stock$date) names(stock)[names(stock) == "FB"] <- "META"  tickers <- c("GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")  fig <- make_subplots(   rows = 3,   cols = 2,   subplot_titles = paste0("company=", tickers),   vertical_spacing = 0.08 ) for (i in seq_along(tickers)) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(       data = stock,       x = ~date,       y = stock[[tickers[[i]]]],       mode = "lines",       fill = "tozeroy",       name = tickers[[i]],       row = (i - 1) %/% 2 + 1,       col = (i - 1) %% 2 + 1     ) }  fig <- fig |>   update_xaxes(showticklabels = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE) |>   update_xaxes(showticklabels = TRUE, title = "date", row = 3) |>   update_yaxes(range = c(0.5, 2)) |>   update_yaxes(title = "value", col = 1) |>   update_yaxes(showticklabels = FALSE, col = 2) |>   update_layout(legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "company"))) |>   update_annotations(font = go_font(size = 10)) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900)  fig

title: Time Series and Date Axes
text: default, tick labels (optional ticks) associated specific grid-line, represent instant time, example, “00:00 February 1, 2018”. Tick labels can formatted using tickformat attribute (accepts d3 time-format formatting strings) display month year, still represent instant default, figure , text label “Feb 2018” spans part month January part month February. dtick attribute controls spacing gridlines, "M1" setting means “1 month”. attribute also accepts number milliseconds, can scaled days multiplying 24*60*60*1000. Note default, formatting values X Y values hover label matches tick labels corresponding axes, customizing tick labels something broad like “month”, ’s usually necessary customize hover label something narrower like actual date, .
code:
library(plotly.core) # Weekly stock prices for 2018-2019, normalized to the first week stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/master/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz" stock <- data.table::fread(stocks_url, data.table = FALSE) stock$date <- as.Date(stock$date) names(stock)[names(stock) == "FB"] <- "META" tickers <- c("GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT") fig <- go_figure() for (tk in tickers) { fig <- fig |> add_scatter(x = stock$date, y = stock[[tk]], mode = "lines", name = tk) } fig <- fig |> update_layout( title = "custom tick labels", legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "variable")), xaxis = go_xaxis(dtick = "M1", tickformat = "%b
%Y") ) |> update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |> update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |> update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900) |> update_layout(width = 1000) fig

what: Moving Tick Labels to the Middle of the Period
title: Time Series and Date Axes
text: new 4.10 setting ticklabelmode attribute "period" (default "instant") can move tick labels middle period represent. gridlines remain beginning month (thanks dtick="M1") labels now span month refer .
code: library(plotly.core)  # Weekly stock prices for 2018-2019, normalized to the first week stocks_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.py/master/plotly/package_data/datasets/stocks.csv.gz" stock <- data.table::fread(stocks_url, data.table = FALSE) stock$date <- as.Date(stock$date) names(stock)[names(stock) == "FB"] <- "META"  tickers <- c("GOOG", "AAPL", "AMZN", "META", "NFLX", "MSFT")  fig <- go_figure() for (tk in tickers) {   fig <- fig |>     add_scatter(x = stock$date, y = stock[[tk]], mode = "lines", name = tk) }  fig <- fig |>   update_layout(     title = "custom tick labels with ticklabelmode=\"period\"",     legend = go_legend(title = go_legend_title(text = "variable")),     xaxis = go_xaxis(dtick = "M1", tickformat = "%b\n%Y", ticklabelmode = "period")   ) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900) |>   update_layout(width = 1000)  fig

title: Time Series and Date Axes
text: Plotly histograms powerful data-aggregation tools even work date axes. figure , pass daily data display monthly averages setting histfunc = "avg" xbins = go_bins(size = "M1").

title: Time Series and Date Axes
text: new 4.11 data coded “January 1” “January 31” fact refers data collected throughout month January, example, can configure traces display marks start end, middle month xperiod xperiodalignment attributes. example , raw data coded X value 10th month, binned monthly periods xperiod="M1" displayed start, middle end period.
code: library(plotly.core)  date <- c(as.Date("2020-01-10"), as.Date("2020-02-10"), as.Date("2020-03-10"),           as.Date("2020-04-10"), as.Date("2020-05-10"), as.Date("2020-06-10")) value <- c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3)  df <- data.frame(date, value)  df |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(     x = ~date,     y = ~value,     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "Raw Data",     marker = go_scatter_marker(symbol = "star")   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = ~date,     y = ~value,     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "Start-aligned",     xperiod = "M1",     xperiodalignment = "start"   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = ~date,     y = ~value,     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "Middle-aligned",     xperiod = "M1",     xperiodalignment = "middle"   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = ~date,     y = ~value,     mode = "lines+markers",     name = "End-aligned",     xperiod = "M1",     xperiodalignment = "end"   ) |>   add_bar(x = ~date, y = ~value, name = "Middle-aligned") |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900)

what: Hover Templates with Mixtures of Period data
title: Time Series and Date Axes
text: New v5.0 displaying periodic data mixed-sized periods (.e. quarterly monthly) conjunction x x unified hovermodes using hovertemplate, xhoverformat attribute can used control period’s X value displayed, special %{xother} hover-template directive can used control X value displayed points share exact X coordinate point hovered . %{xother} return empty string X value one hovered , otherwise return (%{x}). special %{_xother}, %{xother_} %{_xother_} variations display spaces , around parentheses, respectively.
code: library(plotly.core)  go_figure() |>   add_bar(     x = c(as.Date("2020-01-01"), as.Date("2020-04-01"), as.Date("2020-07-01")),     y = c(1000, 1500, 1700),     xperiod = "M3",     xperiodalignment = "middle",     hovertemplate = "%{y}%{_xother}"   ) |>   add_scatter(     x = seq(as.Date("2020-01-01"), as.Date("2020-09-01"), by = "month"),     y = c(1100, 1050, 1200, 1300, 1400, 1700, 1500, 1400, 1600),     mode = "lines+markers",     xperiod = "M1",     xperiodalignment = "middle",     hovertemplate = "%{y}%{_xother}"   ) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900)

code: library(plotly.core)  data <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/finance-charts-apple.csv") data$Date <- as.Date(data$Date)  data |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~Date, y = ~mavg, mode = "lines") |>   update_layout(     xaxis = go_xaxis(       title = "",       rangeslider = go_xaxis_rangeslider(visible = TRUE),       tickformatstops = list(         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list(NULL, 1000), value = "%H:%M:%S.%L ms"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list(1000, 60000), value = "%H:%M:%S s"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list(60000, 3600000), value = "%H:%M m"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list(3600000, 86400000), value = "%H:%M h"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list(86400000, 604800000), value = "%e. %b d"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list(604800000, "M1"), value = "%e. %b w"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list("M1", "M12"), value = "%b '%y M"),         go_tickformatstop(dtickrange = list("M12", NULL), value = "%Y Y")       )     ),     yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "")   ) |>   update_xaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_yaxes(zerolinecolor = "white", zerolinewidth = 2, gridcolor = "white") |>   update_layout(plot_bgcolor = "#e5ecf6", width = 900)

title: Treemap Charts
text: can customize several attributes treemaps create plotly.core, including: values: list values assigned chart sector. textinfo: determines textual information appear chart sector. Valid values text, value, current path, percent root, percent entry, percent parent, combination preceding. pathbar (go_pathbar()): determines whether pathbar visible users zoom chart sectors. branchvalues: method used calculate values chart sectors desendants. Valid values attribute total remainder; default value remainder. set remainder, items values attribute correspond root chart branches sectors taken extra part part sum values leaves. set total, brach’s value taken equal sum values chart sector descendant branch. behavior demonstrated second trace example figure - value Eva branch 65, sum values chart sector descendant branch (14 + 12 + 10 + 2 + 6 + 6 + 1 + 4).
code: library(plotly.core)  labels = c("Eve", "Cain", "Seth", "Enos", "Noam", "Abel", "Awan", "Enoch", "Azura") parents = c("", "Eve", "Eve", "Seth", "Seth", "Eve", "Eve", "Awan", "Eve")  go_figure() |>   add_treemap(     labels = labels,     parents = parents,     values = c(10, 14, 12, 10, 2, 6, 6, 1, 4),     textinfo = "label+value+percent parent+percent entry+percent root",     domain = go_domain(column = 0)   ) |>   add_treemap(     branchvalues = "total",     labels = labels,     parents = parents,     values = c(65, 14, 12, 10, 2, 6, 6, 1, 4),     textinfo = "label+value+percent parent+percent entry",     outsidetextfont = go_font(size = 20, color = "darkblue"),     marker = go_treemap_marker(line = go_treemap_marker_line(width = 2)),     pathbar = go_pathbar(visible = FALSE),     domain = go_domain(column = 1)   ) |>   update_layout(     grid = go_grid(columns = 2, rows = 1),     margin = go_margin(l = 0, r = 0, b = 0, t = 0)   )

title: Treemap Charts
text: three different attributes can use change color sectors treemaps created plotly.core: marker.colors (go_treemap_marker()) marker.colorscale (go_treemap_marker()) treemapcolorway (update_layout()) following examples show use attribute. use marker.colors, pass list valid CSS colors hexadecimal color codes. following example uses marker.colorscale attribute. Rather using list colors, simply supply colorscale. built-colorscales : Greys, YlGnBu, Greens, YlOrRd, Bluered, RdBu, Reds, Blues, Picnic, Rainbow, Portland, Jet, Hot, Blackbody, Earth, Electric, Viridis, Cividis following example uses treemapcolorway attribute, set chart’s layout.
code: library(plotly.core)  labels = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "B1", "B2") parents = c("", "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "", "B1")  go_figure() |>   add_treemap(     labels = labels,     parents = parents,     marker = go_treemap_marker(       colors = c("#000", "royalblue", "lightgray", "purple", "#FFF", "lightgray", "lightblue")     )   ) library(plotly.core)  labels = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "B1", "B2") parents = c("", "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "", "B1") values = c(11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 20, 30)  go_figure() |>   add_treemap(     labels = labels,     parents = parents,     values = values,     marker = go_treemap_marker(colorscale = "Reds")   ) library(plotly.core)  labels = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "B1", "B2") parents = c("", "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "", "B1")  go_figure() |>   add_treemap(labels = labels, parents = parents) |>   update_layout(treemapcolorway = c("pink", "lightgray"))

title: Treemap Charts

what: Controlling Text Font Size with uniformtext
title: Treemap Charts
text: default, font size text labels treemap chart vary fit available space within sector. However, want text labels treemap chart font size, can use uniformtext layout parameter. minsize attribute sets font size, mode attribute sets happens labels fit within sector specified fontsize: either hide show overflow.
code: library(plotly.core) df = read.csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/718417069ead87650b90472464c7565dc8c2cb1c/sunburst-coffee-flavors-complete.csv') df |>   go_figure() |>   add_treemap(ids = ~ids, labels = ~labels, parents = ~parents) |>   update_layout(uniformtext = go_uniformtext(minsize = 10, mode = "hide"))

# one panel per case; x: values plotted, y: the measurement metric_chart <- function(col, label) { # res is sorted by case, size and variant, so each panel's sizes appear in order d <- res[, .(variant, case, label, value = get(col))] # "10 × 100,000" on two lines, so the labels stay horizontal d[, label := sub("10 × ", "10 ×
", label, fixed = TRUE)] cases <- levels(res$case) # R in blues, Python in oranges; the darkest of each is the float32 variant colors <- c(release = "#6baed6", core_backend = "#2171b5", go_figure_f32 = "#08306b", plotly_py = "#fd8d3c", plotly_py_f32 = "#a63603") fig <- make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = length(cases), subplot_titles = cases, horizontal_spacing = 0.02) for (j in seq_along(cases)) { for (v in variants) { dv <- d[case == cases[[j]] & variant == v] if (!nrow(dv)) next fig <- add_bar( fig, x = dv$label, y = dv$value, name = v, legendgroup = v, showlegend = j == 1, marker = go_bar_marker(color = colors[[v]]), row = 1, col = j ) } } fig |> # little margin around the panels (room below for the labels' descenders), # legend above them update_layout( barmode = "group", template = get_template("plotly_white"), margin = go_margin(l = 65, r = 5, t = 25, b = 20), legend = go_legend(orientation = "h", y = 1.08, yanchor = "bottom", x = 0) ) |> # each panel its own sizes, as categories: every bar the same width update_xaxes(type = "category") |> # one y axis shared by the panels, from 0 update_yaxes(matches = "y", rangemode = "tozero") |> update_yaxes(title = label, row = 1, col = 1) |> partial_bundle("auto") } metric_chart("build_sec", "build + write (s)") metric_chart("load_sec", "load (s)") metric_chart("html_mb", "HTML (MB)") metric_chart("peak_renderer_mb", "peak renderer (MB)") metric_chart("js_heap_mb", "JS heap after load (MB)") metric_chart("export_sec", "PNG export (s)")

params$release_lib else file.path(wd, "lib-release") core_lib <- if (nzchar(params$core_lib)) params$core_lib else .libPaths()[1] if ("release" %in% rerun && !file.exists(file.path(release_lib, "plotly", "DESCRIPTION"))) {   dir.create(release_lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   install.packages("plotly", lib = release_lib, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org",                    type = "source", dependencies = FALSE) } libs <- list(release = release_lib, core_backend = core_lib, go_figure_f32 = core_lib) python <- params$python # a partial run (`only`) keeps the other variants' previous results if (partial) {   prev <- lapply(c(build = "build", browser = "browser", pages = "pages", versions = "versions"),                  function(f) fread(file.path(results_dir, paste0(f, ".csv"))))   prev_meta <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(results_dir, "meta.json")) } cases <- rbindlist(list(   data.table(case = "timeseries", size = unlist(params$ts_sizes), values = as.integer(unlist(params$ts_sizes))),   data.table(case = "multiseries", size = unlist(params$ms_sizes), values = as.integer(unlist(params$ms_sizes) * 10)),   data.table(case = "heatmap", size = unlist(params$hm_sizes), values = as.integer(unlist(params$hm_sizes)^2)) )) cases[, file := file.path(wd, "data", sprintf("%s-%d.bin", case, size))] set.seed(2024) for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {   n <- cases$size[i]   v <- if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {     cumsum(rnorm(n))   } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {     as.vector(apply(matrix(rnorm(n * 10), n), 2, cumsum))   } else {     s <- seq(0, 6 * pi, length.out = n)     as.vector(outer(sin(s), cos(s)) + rnorm(n * n, sd = 0.1))   }   writeBin(v, cases$file[i], endian = "little") } figures <- list(   release = list(     timeseries = function(t, y) plot_ly(x = t, y = y, type = "scattergl", mode = "lines"),     multiseries = function(d) {       p <- plot_ly(d, x = ~t)       for (col in names(d)[-1]) {         p <- add_trace(p, y = d[[col]], name = col, type = "scattergl", mode = "lines")       }       p     },     heatmap = function(z) plot_ly(z = z, type = "heatmap")   ),   go_figure_f32 = list(     timeseries = function(t, y) {       go_figure() |> add_scattergl(x = t, y = as_float32(y), mode = "lines")     },     multiseries = function(d) {       fig <- go_figure()       for (col in names(d)[-1]) {         fig <- add_scattergl(fig, x = d$t, y = as_float32(d[[col]]), name = col, mode = "lines")       }       fig     },     heatmap = function(z) go_figure() |> add_heatmap(z = as_float32(z))   ) ) # go_figure() figures load the smallest plotly.js bundle with their trace types figures$go_figure_f32 <- lapply(figures$go_figure_f32, function(make) {   function(...) partial_bundle(make(...)) }) # the same plot_ly() code, run with the development plotly figures$core_backend <- figures$release  # how each variant writes its page writers <- list(   release = function(p, file) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib"),   core_backend = function(p, file) plotly.core::write_html(p, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib"),   go_figure_f32 = function(fig, file) write_html(fig, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib") ) # how each variant exports a static image, with its package's save_image(): # Kaleido (via reticulate) for the CRAN release, Chrome via chromote for # plotly.core (plot_ly() in the development plotly uses plotly.core's). Each # keeps its browser running between images: plotly.core does by itself; # Kaleido is started as a persistent server (by default it starts a browser # for every image, which is slower and failed for some images here), with the # CRAN release's own plotly.js exporters <- list(   release = local({     started <- FALSE     function(p, file) {       if (!started) {         reticulate::import("kaleido")$start_sync_server(           plotlyjs = system.file("htmlwidgets", "lib", "plotlyjs", "plotly-latest.min.js", package = "plotly"),           silence_warnings = TRUE         )         started <<- TRUE       }       plotly::save_image(p, file)     }   }),   core_backend = function(p, file) plotly::save_image(p, file),   go_figure_f32 = function(fig, file) plotly.core::save_image(fig, file) ) import gc, json, sys, time import os import numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly, plotly.io as pio, plotly.graph_objects as go import kaleido # Kaleido with plotly.py's own plotly.js (offline), kept running between images plotlyjs = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(plotly.__file__), "package_data", "plotly.min.js") pio.defaults.plotlyjs = plotlyjs kaleido.start_sync_server(plotlyjs=plotlyjs, silence_warnings=True)  variant, cases_file, reps, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4] f32 = variant == "plotly_py_f32"  def timeseries(t, y):     return go.Figure(go.Scattergl(x=t, y=y, mode="lines"))  def multiseries(t, Y):     fig = go.Figure()     for j in range(Y.shape[1]):         fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(x=t, y=Y[:, j], name=f"y{j + 1:02d}", mode="lines"))     return fig  def heatmap(z):     return go.Figure(go.Heatmap(z=z))  out = [] for case in json.load(open(cases_file)):     n, kind = case["size"], case["case"]     v = np.fromfile(case["file"], dtype="<f8")     if f32:         v = v.astype(np.float32)     if kind == "timeseries":         args = (pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n, freq="s"), v)         make = timeseries     elif kind == "multiseries":         args = (pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n, freq="s"), v.reshape((n, 10), order="F"))         make = multiseries     else:         args = (v.reshape((n, n), order="F"),)         make = heatmap     page = f"{outdir}/{kind}-{n}.html"     save = lambda: make(*args).write_html(page, include_plotlyjs="directory", full_html=True)     save()  # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     fig, png = make(*args), f"{outdir}/{kind}-{n}.png"     fig.write_image(png)  # warm-up     for rep in range(reps):         gc.collect()         t0 = time.perf_counter()         save()         t1 = time.perf_counter()         fig.write_image(png)         out.append(dict(variant=variant, case=kind, size=n, rep=rep + 1,                         build_sec=t1 - t0, export_sec=time.perf_counter() - t1)) kaleido.stop_sync_server(silence_warnings=True) json.dump(out, sys.stdout) r_worker <- function(variant, fns, write, export, cases, reps, outdir) {   suppressPackageStartupMessages(     if (variant == "go_figure_f32") library(plotly.core) else library(plotly)   )   dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   out <- list()   for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {     n <- cases$size[i]     v <- readBin(cases$file[i], "double", n = cases$values[i], endian = "little")     t <- as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC") + seq_len(n) - 1     if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {       args <- list(t = t, y = v)     } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {       y <- matrix(v, n, 10, dimnames = list(NULL, sprintf("y%02d", 1:10)))       args <- list(d = data.table::data.table(t = t, y))     } else {       args <- list(z = matrix(v, n, n))     }     make <- fns[[cases$case[i]]]     page <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.html", cases$case[i], n))     save <- function() write(do.call(make, args), page)     save() # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     # static image export of a figure made beforehand, so only the export is timed     fig <- do.call(make, args)     png <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.png", cases$case[i], n))     export(fig, png) # warm-up     for (rep in seq_len(reps)) {       gc()       out[[length(out) + 1]] <- list(         variant = variant, case = cases$case[i], size = n, rep = rep,         build_sec = system.time(save())[["elapsed"]],         export_sec = system.time(export(fig, png))[["elapsed"]]       )     }   }   data.table::rbindlist(out) }  # Kaleido (for the CRAN release) runs in the benchmark's Python, which also # has plotly; ~/.Renviron is skipped, as it may point reticulate elsewhere worker_env <- c(callr::rcmd_safe_env(), RETICULATE_PYTHON = python, R_ENVIRON_USER = tempfile()) build_r <- rbindlist(lapply(intersect(names(figures), rerun), function(v) {   callr::r(r_worker, list(v, figures[[v]], writers[[v]], exporters[[v]], cases, reps, file.path(pages_dir, v)),            libpath = c(libs[[v]], .libPaths()), env = worker_env) })) cases_json <- file.path(wd, "cases.json") jsonlite::write_json(cases[, .(case, size, file)], cases_json) build_py <- rbindlist(lapply(intersect(c("plotly_py", "plotly_py_f32"), rerun), function(v) {   outdir <- file.path(pages_dir, v)   dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE)   res <- system2(python, c(shQuote(file.path(wd, "bench.py")), v, shQuote(cases_json), reps,                            shQuote(outdir)), stdout = TRUE)   as.data.table(jsonlite::fromJSON(paste(res, collapse = ""))) })) build <- rbindlist(list(build_r, build_py)) # one page per variant and case size pages <- CJ(variant = rerun, i = seq_len(nrow(cases)), sorted = FALSE)[   , c(.(variant = variant), cases[i, .(case, size, values)])] pages[, path := sprintf("%s/%s-%d.html", variant, case, size)] pages[, html_mb := file.size(file.path(pages_dir, path)) / 1e6] (function () {   var B = window.__bench = { done: false };   function finish() {     if (B.end != null) return;     B.end = performance.now();     requestAnimationFrame(function () {       setTimeout(function () { B.painted = performance.now(); B.done = true; }, 0);     });   }   // plotly.js 3+ exports are read-only, so the wrapper is a new object   // inheriting from Plotly, with timed newPlot()/react()/plot()   function wrap(P) {     if (!P || P.__benchWrapped) return P;     var W = Object.create(P);     ["newPlot", "react", "plot"].forEach(function (k) {       var orig = P[k];       if (typeof orig !== "function") return;       W[k] = function () {         if (B.start == null) B.start = performance.now();         var r = orig.apply(P, arguments);         Promise.resolve(r).then(finish, function (e) { B.error = String(e); B.done = true; });         return r;       };     });     W.__benchWrapped = true;     return W;   }   var plotly;   Object.defineProperty(window, "Plotly", {     configurable: true,     get: function () { return plotly; },     set: function (v) { plotly = wrap(v); }   });   window.addEventListener("error", function (e) { B.error = String(e.message); B.done = true; }); })(); hook_js <- paste(readLines(file.path(wd, "hook.js")), collapse = "\n") chrome <- chromote::Chromote$new()  # serve the pages over HTTP from localhost port <- httpuv::randomPort() server <- callr::r_bg(function(dir, port) httpuv::runStaticServer(dir, port = port, browse = FALSE),                       list(pages_dir, port)) for (i in 1:50) {   if (!inherits(try(suppressWarnings(readLines(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/", port), n = 1)),                     silent = TRUE), "try-error")) break   Sys.sleep(0.1) }  # samples the largest renderer process's memory (RSS) every 20 ms until killed sampler <- function(browser_pid, out) {   peak <- 0   writeLines("0", out) # started   repeat {     procs <- try(ps::ps_children(ps::ps_handle(browser_pid), recursive = TRUE), silent = TRUE)     if (!inherits(procs, "try-error")) {       for (p in procs) {         rss <- try({           if (any(grepl("--type=renderer", ps::ps_cmdline(p), fixed = TRUE))) ps::ps_memory_info(p)[["rss"]] else 0         }, silent = TRUE)         if (is.numeric(rss) && rss > peak) {           peak <- rss           writeLines(format(peak, scientific = FALSE), out)         }       }     }     Sys.sleep(0.02)   } } browser_pid <- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid()  measure_page <- function(url, timeout = 300) {   s <- chromote::ChromoteSession$new(parent = chrome, width = 1000, height = 600)   on.exit(s$close(), add = TRUE)   s$Network$enable()   s$Network$setCacheDisabled(cacheDisabled = TRUE)   s$Page$enable() # needed for the injected script to run   s$Page$addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument(source = hook_js)   peak_file <- tempfile()   smp <- callr::r_bg(sampler, list(browser_pid, peak_file))   on.exit(smp$kill(), add = TRUE)   # wait for the sampler to start   for (i in 1:100) if (file.exists(peak_file)) break else Sys.sleep(0.05)   Sys.sleep(0.1)   s$Page$navigate(url, wait_ = FALSE) # large pages can take a while to commit   t0 <- Sys.time()   repeat {     done <- s$Runtime$evaluate("!!(window.__bench && window.__bench.done)", timeout_ = timeout)$result$value     if (isTRUE(done)) break     if (difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs") > timeout) stop("timed out loading ", url)     Sys.sleep(0.05)   }   Sys.sleep(0.3)   smp$kill()   b <- jsonlite::fromJSON(s$Runtime$evaluate(     "JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, window.__bench, {js_bytes: performance.getEntriesByType('resource')        .filter(e => /\\.js$/.test(e.name)).reduce((a, e) => a + e.encodedBodySize, 0)}))"   )$result$value)   if (!is.null(b$error)) stop(url, ": ", b$error)   s$HeapProfiler$collectGarbage()   heap <- s$Runtime$getHeapUsage()   data.table(     load_sec = b$painted / 1000,     newplot_sec = (b$end - b$start) / 1000,     js_mb = b$js_bytes / 1e6,     peak_renderer_mb = as.numeric(readLines(peak_file, warn = FALSE)) / 1e6,     js_heap_mb = (heap$usedSize + if (is.null(heap$backingStorageSize)) 0 else heap$backingStorageSize) / 1e6   ) }  restart_chrome <- function() {   try(chrome$close(), silent = TRUE)   chrome <<- chromote::Chromote$new()   browser_pid <<- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid() } # on a failure (e.g. Chrome not responding), restart Chrome and try the page # once more; a page that fails twice (e.g. too large to load) is recorded as # missing values, and not tried again in later rounds failed <- character() measure_retry <- function(url) {   missing <- data.table(load_sec = NA_real_, newplot_sec = NA_real_, js_mb = NA_real_,                         peak_renderer_mb = NA_real_, js_heap_mb = NA_real_)   if (url %in% failed) return(missing)   for (attempt in 1:2) {     r <- tryCatch(measure_page(url), error = identity)     if (!inherits(r, "error")) return(r)     message("attempt ", attempt, " at ", url, " failed: ", conditionMessage(r))     restart_chrome()   }   failed <<- c(failed, url)   missing }  set.seed(1) browser <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(reps), function(rep) {   # shuffle the page order each round, so drift doesn't favour a variant   rbindlist(lapply(sample(nrow(pages)), function(i) {     cbind(pages[i, .(variant, case, size)], rep = rep,           measure_retry(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/%s", port, pages$path[i])))   })) })) server$kill() r_versions <- function(lib) {   callr::r(function() {     js_version <- function(pkg, file) {       f <- system.file("htmlwidgets", "lib", "plotlyjs", file, package = pkg)       if (!nzchar(f)) return(NA_character_)       head <- readChar(f, 500)       sub("^v", "", regmatches(head, regexpr("v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", head)))     }     # the development plotly draws with plotly.core's plotly.js     uses_core <- grepl("plotly.core", utils::packageDescription("plotly")$Imports, fixed = TRUE)     list(       plotly = as.character(utils::packageVersion("plotly")),       plotly.core = if (uses_core) as.character(utils::packageVersion("plotly.core")) else NA,       plotly.js = if (uses_core) js_version("plotly.core", "plotly.min.js") else js_version("plotly", "plotly-latest.min.js")     )   }, libpath = c(lib, .libPaths())) } py_rerun <- any(c("plotly_py", "plotly_py_f32") %in% rerun) if (py_rerun) {   py <- jsonlite::fromJSON(system2(python, c("-c", shQuote(paste(     "import json, plotly, numpy, pandas, plotly.offline as o;",     "print(json.dumps(dict(plotly=plotly.__version__, numpy=numpy.__version__,",     "pandas=pandas.__version__, plotlyjs=o.get_plotlyjs_version())))"))), stdout = TRUE)) } versions <- rbindlist(list(   if ("release" %in% rerun) c(variant = "release", r_versions(release_lib)),   if (any(c("core_backend", "go_figure_f32") %in% rerun)) {     c(variant = "core_backend, go_figure_f32", r_versions(core_lib))   },   if (py_rerun) {     list(variant = "plotly_py, plotly_py_f32",          plotly = paste0(py$plotly, " (Python; numpy ", py$numpy, ", pandas ", py$pandas, ")"),          plotly.core = NA_character_, plotly.js = py$plotlyjs)   } ), fill = TRUE) cpu <- if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Darwin") {   system("sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string", intern = TRUE) } else {   NA_character_ } meta <- list(date = format(Sys.Date()), R = R.version.string, os = utils::sessionInfo()$running,              cpu = cpu, browser = chrome$Browser$getVersion()$product, reps = reps) chrome$close()  pages <- pages[, .(variant, case, size, values, html_mb)] if (partial) {   # the other variants' previous results, for the same cases   if (!setequal(paste(prev$pages$case, prev$pages$size), paste(cases$case, cases$size))) {     stop("A partial run (`only`) needs the same case sizes as the saved results", call. = FALSE)   }   keep <- function(d) d[!variant %in% rerun]   build <- rbind(keep(prev$build), build, fill = TRUE)   browser <- rbind(keep(prev$browser), browser, fill = TRUE)   pages <- rbind(keep(prev$pages), pages, fill = TRUE)   versions <- rbind(prev$versions[!variant %in% versions$variant], versions, fill = TRUE)   versions <- versions[order(match(sub(",.*", "", variant), variants))]   meta$rerun <- rerun   meta$previous_date <- prev_meta$previous_date %||% prev_meta$date }  fwrite(build, file.path(results_dir, "build.csv")) fwrite(browser, file.path(results_dir, "browser.csv")) fwrite(pages, file.path(results_dir, "pages.csv")) fwrite(versions, file.path(results_dir, "versions.csv")) jsonlite::write_json(meta, file.path(results_dir, "meta.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

title: Rendering performance
text: Three use cases, range sizes: Large time series: one scattergl line trace date-time x (1 s steps) random walk y. 10 time series: ten scattergl line traces, one per column wide data.table, sharing date-time x. plotly.core sends array repeated figure (see widget_to_JSON()), x sent rather ten times. Large matrix heatmap: one heatmap trace n × n matrix. Metrics: Build + write (s): R Python time figure-making call standalone HTML page written disk (htmlwidgets::saveWidget() CRAN release, plotly.core’s write_html() plot_ly() development plotly go_figure(), fig.write_html() Python), one untimed warm-run, fresh process per variant. Image export (s): time save figure, made beforehand, 700 × 500 PNG package’s export (save_image() R; fig.write_image() plotly.py), one untimed warm-export, process build timings. covers converting figure JSON (including plotly_build() plot_ly() figures, built exported), drawing headless browser writing PNG; starting browser (done warm-, 1–1.5 s session’s first image) , go_figure() plotly.py, creating figure object. Kaleido (CRAN plotly, plotly.py) runs persistent server package’s plotly.js, plotly.core keeps Chrome running. HTML (MB): size page, holds figure data (plotly.js separate file). Load time (s): headless Chrome, navigation start first frame painted plotly.js’s newPlot() resolves. Pages served HTTP localhost browser cache disabled, time covers fetching parsing plotly.js page, decoding data plotting, network latency. newPlot (s): time plotly.js spends newPlot(), part load time. Peak renderer memory (MB): largest resident memory page’s renderer process loading, sampled every 20 ms. JS heap load (MB): JavaScript heap use load forced garbage collection, plus array buffers (Chrome reports ).
